kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.

name: Global Room
description: The Trinity Global Room is a welcoming student support hub and event space on campus for all Trinity students, assisting students to settle into life at Trinity and Dublin. The Global Room professional team, supported by a team of Student Ambassadors, is available to help students with a wide range of queries, from immigration and accommodation to general advice on living in Dublin. Each year, over 300 events take place in the Global Room, many of which focus on cultural celebrations and social meet-ups for students. When events are not taking place, students are welcome to use the space to meet friends, have lunch, study or simply relax, either on their own or in small groups. To support these different activities, the Global Room offcers different seating spaces, from tables and chairs, couches, high stools, and TCD Sense seating.
food_drink_allowed_note: Feel free to bring your own food and beverages into the Global Room. While there are no facilities to prepare food, you are welcome to enjoy your snacks and drinks in this space.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
wheelchair_note:
The Global Room is fully accessible to students. Located on the first floor of the Watts Building, next to the Academic Registry, the space is designed to be inclusive and accommodating to all students.

There is an accessible toilet outside the Global Room, and more toilets can be found downstairs in the Watts Building.
seating_note: The Global Room offers a variety of seating options to accommodate different needs. Comfortable couches, armchairs, and communal tables provide spaces for relaxation, socialising, and studying either in small groups or individually.
outlets_note: Numerous plug sockets are available throughout the Global Room, ensuring you can easily charge your devices while you relax or work.
sense_exp: While events are taking place, the Global Room can be a vibrant and noisy space, however the recent installation of soundproofing has helped to dampen the sound. Outside of events, the Global Room provides balanced environment, offering students choice in seating areas that suit their sensory preferences.
wayfinding:
The Global Room is conveniently located beside the Academic Registry on the first floor of the Watts Building. Clear signage throughout the Hamilton Building will help direct you.

[Youtube Video]https://youtu.be/lIO5E9jY3Kc)
phys_access: The Global Room offers a versatile and welcoming physical environment. Designed to accommodate approximately 80 people, the space includes various seating options, workspaces, and areas for social interaction. The layout encourages a community feel while also providing spots for individual or small group activities.

kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.

further_info:
[TCDSense, Trinity's Sensory Processing Project.](https://www.tcd.ie/disability/services/tcdsense.php) 

TCDSense aims to make Trinity College Dublin more inclusive, by creating a variety of different sensory environments to meet the needs of all students and staff across the various Trinity campuses. This involves reviewing and improving new and existing spaces across Trinity, creating increased awareness of the sensory environment amongst students and staff, and delivering specialist supports to students who need more support in managing and adapting the existing sensory environments of college.

name: The Forum
description: The Forum Restaurant in Trinity Business School offers a sleek, modern space where students can enjoy a meal, socialise, or catch up on some work. The area is designed with contemporary aesthetics, featuring clean lines, stylish furniture, and a bright, welcoming atmosphere. It's an ideal spot for both casual dining and productive meetings, providing a versatile environment that caters to various needs throughout the day.
food_drink_allowed_note: As a restaurant, The Forum serves a variety of food and drinks, with options available for breakfast, lunch, and snacks throughout the day. Students are welcome to purchase meals and beverages on-site, and enjoy them at their leisure within the seating areas.
wheelchair_note: This space is fully accessible to all students. The building features level entry points, and the seating arrangement is designed to accommodate easy movement and accessibility.
seating_note: The restaurant is well-equipped with numerous chairs and tables, offering ample space for dining, studying, or socialising. The seating is comfortable and varied, ensuring that whether you're in the mood for a quick bite or an extended study session, you'll find a suitable spot.
outlets_note: While primarily a dining space, The Forum Restaurant also caters to students who need to charge their devices while they work. There are several plug sockets available around the seating areas, making it convenient to stay powered up.
sense_exp: The Forum Restaurant offers a vibrant sensory experience with its modern design, bright lighting, and the lively buzz of a busy dining area. The sleek, clean lines of the furniture, combined with the warm colours and textures, create a stimulating yet comfortable environment. The aroma of freshly prepared food and the background hum of conversation make it an inviting space to spend time in.
wayfinding:
The Forum Restaurant is located within Trinity Business School, easily accessible from the main entrance.

Once inside the building's main entrance look left and you should see signage on the ground floor.

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/l6wnBqaBxyU)
phys_access: The Forum Restaurant is on the ground floor of Trinity Business School, with accessible entrances and pathways leading directly to the dining area. The layout is spacious, allowing for easy movement, and the tables are positioned to accommodate wheelchair users and those with other mobility needs. This ensures that all students can comfortably enjoy the space, whether they're dining, working, or socialising.

opening_times.note: Open until 6pm on Mon & Tue, and until 4pm on Wed & Thur.

name: Benches on the Green
description: The Benches on the Green offer a serene outdoor social space located in a square ring around a large green area. This tranquil spot is situated between the Fitzgerald and Chemistry buildings, providing a perfect place to relax, study, or enjoy a meal in the fresh air.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring your own food and drink to this space. It's an ideal spot for a picnic or a break between classes.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: The area is accessible to all students. However, since the benches are located on grass, there is a possibility of mud, especially after rain, which might make it challenging for some students to navigate.
seating_note: There are many wooden benches arranged in a square ring, offering ample seating options for students to enjoy.
outlets_note: There are no plug sockets available outdoors.
sense_exp: The green area is generally peaceful, with natural sounds providing a calming atmosphere. However, this can change depending on the number of people present.
wayfinding: The Benches on the Green are located between the Fitzgerald and Chemistry buildings. Look for the large green area with a square ring of benches.
phys_access: The area is designed to be accessible to all students, but the grassy terrain can become muddy, which might pose a challenge. The benches themselves are easily accessible once you reach the green.

opening_times.note: This area is outside and is subject to Campus closing times.

name: St. James' ZML
description: The St. James' Hospital Zón Mac Léinn, is a dedicated student area located on the first floor of the building. It provides a welcoming environment for students to relax, eat, and socialise. The space is furnished with a variety of seating options, from colourful and neutral sofas to tables, and is adorned with artwork that adds a touch of creativity and calm. The room is partitioned into two sections, offering flexibility for group gatherings or more private study sessions. The natural lighting and green foliage contribute to a peaceful atmosphere, making it an ideal space for unwinding between classes.
food_drink_allowed_note: Yes, food and drink are allowed in this space. With six microwaves and two kettles available, it's a convenient spot for heating up meals or making a hot drink. The area is designed with students in mind, providing a comfortable place to enjoy your food.
microwave_note: Six microwaves are available in the St. James' Hospital Social Space, making it easy for students to heat their meals. There is also a sink for cleaning up afterwards.
kettle_note: A kettle is available for students to use, making it convenient to prepare hot drinks like tea or coffee.
wheelchair_note: The social space is accessible to all students, with both stair and lift access to the first floor. While the front door of the building operates on a push/pull system and is not fully accessible, the internal door to the Old Stone Building has an automatic button system for ease of access. However, the doors to the common room itself are push/pull.
seating_note: There are plenty of seating options available in the social space. The first room features vibrant, colourful sofas, while the second room offers more neutral-toned sofas. There are also tables where you can sit comfortably to enjoy a meal or do some light work.
outlets_note: The social space is equipped with multiple power outlets, ensuring you can charge your devices or use your laptop while relaxing in the area.
sense_exp: The space offers a calming sensory experience. The walls are painted a light blue, contributing to a tranquil atmosphere, while the natural, dim lighting enhances the space's peaceful ambience. Green foliage adds a touch of nature, and the space is divided into two rooms—one with colourful sofas and another with neutral tones—allowing students to choose the environment that best suits their mood. The outside corridor, with skylight windows, is warm and filled with natural sunlight.
wayfinding: To find the Social Space, enter the building and take the stairs or lift to the first floor. Once upstairs, the social space is adjacent to gendered and accessible toilets, with a prayer room located on the same floor. For refreshments, vending and coffee machines can be found on the ground floor.
phys_access: The building offers ramp access for ease of entry, and the internal door to the equipped with an automatic button system. However, the main entrance door requires manual operation, which may pose challenges for some students. The social space and common room has a push/pull doors which may also require assistance. Despite these limitations, the space is designed to be as inclusive as possible, with accessible toilets available on the same floor.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)

name: Social Pods
description: The Business School Pods offer a versatile social and study environment within the upper levels of the Business School building. These pods are designed to provide a variety of seating arrangements and spaces for both collaborative and individual activities. The area features a range of seating options and is ideal for students looking to work, meet, or relax.
food_drink_allowed_note: Students are permitted to bring food and drinks into the pods. The space is designed to accommodate casual dining and socialising.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: The Business School Pods are accessible to all students. The pods are located on the upper levels of the building and can be reached via lifts.
seating_note: The Business School Pods include a mix of seating arrangements such as modular sofas, individual chairs, and small group seating. There are also informal lounges and study pods equipped with comfortable seating, ideal for both group discussions and quiet work.
outlets_note: Multiple power outlets are provided throughout the pods to ensure that students can charge their electronic devices while using the space.
sense_exp: The sensory experience in the pods varies depending on the specific area. Some pods offer bright, natural lighting, while others provide a more subdued atmosphere with ambient lighting. The space is designed to be comfortable and conducive to both focused work and social interactions.

kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.

name: Douglas Hyde Gallery
description:
A unique space to see and learn about contemporary art, open five days a week and admission is always free.
Explore the current exhibitions, artist talks, screenings and workshops or delve into various programmes for young people or the rich archive of exhibitions and events.

The Douglas Hyde Gallery of Contemporary Art was co-founded in a unique partnership between the Arts Council of Ireland and Trinity College Dublin. It opened to the public in March 1978 as the first publicly funded space dedicated to contemporary art and the first university gallery in Ireland. Throughout its history, the Douglas Hyde has presented pivotal exhibitions by Irish artists and brought artists of significant international.

We believe that art plays a central role in shaping the world we live in, and that galleries are an essential public space in a progressive society. As an institution we value excellence, enquiry, experimentation and diversity. Art deepens our understanding of ourselves and gives us new ways of thinking and of seeing the world.

kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.

opening_times.note: Opening based on Exhibitions, please see The Douglas Hyde website.

name: Outdoor Seating
description: The Outdoor Seating area is situated between the Old Stone Building and the St. James Centre for Health Sciences. This tranquil outdoor space offers a peaceful retreat from the bustle of campus life. It is an ideal spot for students and staff to relax, socialise, or enjoy a break amidst a pleasant outdoor setting.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring your own refreshments or enjoy snacks purchased from nearby campus facilities. The open-air setting makes it a great spot for casual dining or enjoying a coffee break.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the Old Stone Building Common Room.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the Old Stone Building Common Room.
wheelchair_note:
The Outdoor Seating area is accessible to all students. The space is designed to be inclusive, with pathways and seating arrangements that accommodate wheelchairs and other mobility aids. 

There is also an accessible picnic bench available.
seating_note: The area features a variety of outdoor seating options, including benches and individual chairs. These are arranged to provide both communal and solitary spaces, allowing users to choose their preferred level of interaction or privacy. The seating is designed to be durable and comfortable, suitable for various weather conditions.
sense_exp: The area benefits from ample natural light and a pleasant outdoor atmosphere. The surroundings are characterised by greenery and the natural elements of the campus landscape, contributing to a refreshing and calming environment.
wayfinding: To locate the Outdoor Seating area, head towards the space between the Old Stone building and the St. James Centre for Health Sciences. The seating area is easily accessible from both buildings and is situated in a visible and open location.

kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the Old Stone Building Common Room.

sense_exp: If you prefer minimal visual stimuli while studying, this area has a mix of three enclosed pods and some flexible seating. Additionally there are bookable rooms with this library.

name: SU Cistin
description: The SU Kitchen, located within the Teach 6, is a cosy and functional space designed for students to prepare and enjoy their meals, socialise, or take a well-deserved break. The kitchen is equipped with essential amenities, including microwaves, kettles, and a toaster, making it easy to heat up food or prepare a hot drink. Large windows flood the space with natural, bright light, creating a welcoming atmosphere. However, being situated beside the busy sabbatical office space and overlooking Front Square, the area can become lively and loud during peak hours. Despite its central location, the SU Kitchen remains a popular spot for students looking for a convenient and comfortable place to relax.
food_drink_allowed_note: Yes, food and drink are allowed. With two microwaves, a toaster, and kettles provided, it’s an ideal space for students bringing their own meals. You’ll also find a sink for washing up and cutlery and mugs available for use.
microwave_note: Two microwaves are availabe, allowing students to quickly and conveniently heat up their meals. The space is well-suited for those who prefer to bring their own food to campus.
kettle_note: A kettle is available for students to use, making it convenient to prepare hot drinks like tea or coffee.
wheelchair_note: Unfortunately, the SU Kitchen is not fully accessible to all students. The Teach 6 building lacks lift access, and while there is a ramp for entering the building, the kitchen itself is located on a floor that requires stair access.
seating_note: The space offers ample seating options, including six comfortable sofas for lounging, as well as tables for dining or studying. Whether you’re catching up with friends over lunch or simply taking a moment to yourself, the seating is designed to accommodate a variety of needs.
outlets_note: There are several power outlets available throughout the kitchen, ensuring that you can charge your devices or work on your laptop while enjoying the space.
sense_exp: The sensory experience is shaped by its natural, bright lighting, thanks to large windows that allow plenty of sunlight to enter. While the light creates a pleasant and energising environment, the proximity to the sabbatical office space and the view of the bustling Front Square can lead to higher noise levels, particularly during busy times of the day. This makes the kitchen a vibrant, albeit sometimes noisy, place to be.
wayfinding:
To find the SU Kitchen within Teach 6, enter the building via the main entrance. Once inside go up the stairs to the 1st floor and find the signposted door on the left.

There is no lift to this space.
phys_access: The SU Kitchen, while well-equipped and centrally located, is not fully accessible. The building has ramp access, but the kitchen itself is on a floor that can only be reached by stairs, as there is no lift. This lack of full accessibility may be a barrier for some students. The space is otherwise well-appointed with all necessary amenities.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)

name: Seating Pods
description: There is a new seating pod on the 2nd floor of the Hamilton Building just outside the Hamilton Library.  This provides a space with excellent natural light with some background ambient noise.
food_drink_allowed_note: Feel free to bring along your snacks and beverages. The Hamilton Building encourages a study-friendly environment where you can keep hydrated and energised with your own food and drink.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
wheelchair_note: The sensory pods are not wheelchair accessible due to being raised.
seating_note: The sensory pods come equipped with comfortable bench seating arrangements to ensure a pleasant and ergonomic study experience. Whether you're here for a quick review session or an extended study period, the seating is designed to support your posture and minimise discomfort.
outlets_note: Each sensory pod is fitted with multiple plug sockets, allowing you to charge your devices easily. Whether you need to power up your laptop, phone, or tablet, you'll find sufficient outlets to keep your devices running throughout your study session.
sense_exp: The sensory pod is designed to provide a serene and distraction-free study environment. With features such as noise reduction panels, adjustable lighting, and comfortable seating, these pods aim to enhance focus and reduce sensory overload. Whether you prefer dim lighting or a brighter setting, you can customise your pod to suit your preferences.
wayfinding: The pod is located outside the Hamilton Library on the 2nd floor.

name: JCR Hamilton Quiet Rooms
description: Within the JCR Hamilton student space, several small enclosed rooms are designated as Quiet Spaces. These rooms provide a tranquil environment where students can rest, study, or socialize in a calm setting while still being in the heart of one of the campus's largest student zones. These Quiet Spaces are perfect for those seeking a peaceful retreat amidst their busy schedules.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring your own food and beverages into the Quiet Spaces. While there are no facilities to prepare food within these rooms, you can enjoy your snacks and drinks in this serene environment.
microwave_note: There are 4 microwaves available in the JCR Hamilton, allowing you to heat up your meals and enjoy hot food during your time in the space.
kettle_note: A kettle is available in the JCR Hamilton for students to use, making it convenient to prepare hot drinks like tea or coffee.
wheelchair_note: The Quiet Spaces are located on the ground floor of the JCR Hamilton, ensuring accessibility for all students. Some rooms may feature narrower doorways or tight manoeuvring spaces, however, there is accessible seating arrangements to accommodate all students.
seating_note: The Quiet Spaces offer comfortable seating options designed for relaxation and focus. Each room is equipped with ergonomic chairs and desks, ensuring that students can work or rest comfortably.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are available in each Quiet Space, allowing you to charge your electronic devices conveniently. Whether you need to power your laptop for studying or charge your phone, you'll find easily accessible outlets.
sense_exp: The Quiet Spaces offer a calming sensory experience with features such as soft lighting and sound-reducing elements. These rooms are designed to minimise distractions and create a peaceful atmosphere conducive to rest, study, and quiet social interaction.
wayfinding: The Quiet Spaces are located within the JCR Hamilton on the ground floor. They can be found frequently, but mostly towards the back end of the area. There is signage indicating designated quiet rooms.
phys_access: The Quiet Spaces provide a comfortable and supportive physical environment. With ergonomic seating, soft lighting, and sound-reducing elements, these rooms are designed to help you relax and focus. The layout of each room ensures a peaceful atmosphere, making them ideal for individual study, relaxation, or quiet socialisation.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/))

name: Oldham House
description: Oldham house provides a number of lovely sensory spaces with a variety of seating including enclosed chairs, couches, and rocking chairs. The rooms at the front of Oldham House provide very nice natural light from the big bay windows.  Spaces can be used as social or study spaces when quiet. There is a library upstairs with seating for 16 students for quiet study. Access to Oldham House is from 8.00am to 11.30pm. Residents wishing to hold functions and events can book various rooms and areas throughout the communal social space.  The upper floors are served by a main central staircase and are therefore inaccessible to wheelchair users. The building comprises of common rooms, leisure facilities and an assembly hall. There are additional social spaces at the back of Oldham house with two pool tables.

name: Sensory Pods
description: The sensory pods, located in the basement of the Eavan Boland Library, provide a tranquil environment for individual study. Designed to offer a quiet, focused space, these pods have acoustic protection to minimise ambient noise and create a calming atmosphere. Each pod is equipped with controls that allow students to adjust the lighting levels and airflow according to their needs, offering a personalised study experience. These pods are ideal for those seeking a distraction-free zone to work on assignments or read in peace.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drinks are not permitted inside the sensory pods to maintain cleanliness and avoid distractions for other users.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The sensory pods are technically accessible for all students, including those using wheelchairs. The doors are semi-automatic, with no lip at ground level, allowing easier access. However, the doors are not fully automated, and the presence of a chair inside the room might limit space for those who need additional room to manoeuvre.
seating_note: Each sensory pod includes a comfortable chair designed for long study sessions. However, students should be aware that the chair may occupy space in the pod, which might limit movement for those requiring a more open layout.
outlets_note: There are plug sockets available inside the pods for students to charge their laptops, tablets, and other devices while they study.
sense_exp: These pods are specifically designed to provide a sensory-controlled environment. The acoustic insulation blocks out much of the surrounding noise, and the user-controlled lighting and airflow panels allow students to create a study space that best suits their sensory preferences. The environment is quiet and peaceful, making it ideal for students who are sensitive to sensory stimuli or need a calm space to focus.
wayfinding:
The sensory pods are located in the basement of the Eavan Boland Library. Upon entering the library, take the stairs or lift down to the basement level.

You can use the internal library complex navigation tool to find this space and see how to get to it from one of the many entrances to the library complex.

You can find the location of the space within the library [here](https://app.cloudpano.com/tours/_JKNOIx10eo?sceneId=K72FZNQs96).
further_info:
You can book this space on the library page: [BOOK HERE](https://tcd-ie.libcal.com/reserve/sensorypods)

For more information on the Boland Library, including library services and more, you can contact the library directly or visit the website:

Email: library@tcd.ie

Website: [Library Site](https://www.tcd.ie/library/)

The Boland Library is part of the larger Boland-Lecky-Ussher Complex, providing a comprehensive range of resources and study environments to support your academic journey.

The Eavan Boland Library was named after Irish Poet Eavan Boland in October 2024. The library was previously known as the Berkeley Library.

opening_times.note: Can be booked, see end of page.

College Park is located at the east end of college in front of the Pavilion bar. 
The green space serves as the central area for outdoor sports and recreational activities, including cricket, soccer, hockey, and athletics. 
College Park is not only a hub for sports but also a tranquil spot for students and visitors, enhancing the campus's aesthetic and community life.
wheelchair_note: College Park is accessible from all sides.
seating_note: Seating is available along the sides of the park

A tarmac path encircles College Park, providing access to a car park located on one side, as well as benches positioned on the opposite side.

name: Trinity Botanic Gardens
description: The Botanic Garden is a quiet and peaceful space for the college community to enjoy the nature and an incredible collection of plants. During term time some areas may be slightly busy when they are being used for teaching, but most of the time they are quiet and peaceful. Visitors are welcome to walk the grounds, explore the glasshouses, or rest, read and relax with nature. name: Knowledge Exchange
description: The TBSI Knowledge Exchange is a vibrant social space located within the Trinity Biomedical Sciences Institute (TBSI). This area is designed for relaxation and informal gatherings, offering a comfortable environment for students and staff alike. With an array of couches and seating options, it's an ideal spot for taking a break, catching up with friends, or engaging in collaborative discussions. The space is complemented by a coffee dock area and several amenities to enhance your experience.
food_drink_allowed_note: Students are welcome to bring their own food and drink into the Knowledge Exchange. With the coffee dock area nearby, you can easily grab a coffee or tea to enjoy with your meal. The space is equipped with microwaves and kettles, allowing you to heat up your food or prepare a hot drink on the spot.
microwave_note: There are multiple microwaves, making it easy for students to heat up their meals. Whether you’re bringing lunch from home or just need to warm up a quick snack, the facilities are readily available.
kettle_note: There are kettles available at this space.
wheelchair_note: The Knowledge Exchange is fully accessible to all students. The doors to the location are automated, and a lift is used to get onto the second floor of the building.
seating_note: This space is furnished with numerous couches and seating arrangements, providing a relaxed atmosphere for students to unwind or engage in conversation. Whether you’re looking to lounge on a couch or find a more upright seat for a quick chat, there’s a spot for everyone.
outlets_note: There are several plug sockets available throughout this space, making it convenient for students to charge their devices while they relax or work.
sense_exp: The atmosphere in the Knowledge Exchange is both lively and comfortable. The space is filled with natural light, creating a warm and inviting environment. The presence of couches and soft seating helps to absorb noise, making it a pleasant place to relax even when busy. The coffee dock area adds a comforting aroma of fresh coffee, enhancing the overall sensory experience.
wayfinding: Wayfinding for Space 1
phys_access: The Knowledge Exchange is situated within the fully accessible TBSI. The building features lifts and ramps, ensuring that all students can easily reach the space. The layout of the Knowledge Exchange itself is designed to accommodate everyone, with wide pathways and easily navigable seating arrangements.

name: High Back Seating 2nd, 3rd, 4th Floor
description: Numerous feedback surveys have highlighted that students value natural light, flexible seating and a connection to nature in their study environment. We have installed over thirty high-backed enclosed seats of various shapes, fabrics and colours throughout the libraries, in areas that provide these sensory characteristics.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wayfinding: Please see location here and each floor above: https://wagnerguide.com/c/trinitycollegedublin/ussher?animation=19041
further_info:
[TCDSense, Trinity's Sensory Processing Project.](https://www.tcd.ie/disability/services/tcdsense.php)

name: Stone Benches
description:
A series of stone benches in front of the SNIAM building.

This tranquil outdoor space is adorned with a variety of interesting plants, thanks to its proximity to the Botany department. The area offers a serene environment that is generally quieter than other parts of the campus, making it an ideal spot for relaxation or contemplation.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring your own food and drink to the Stone Benches. Enjoy a picnic or simply have a snack while taking in the peaceful atmosphere.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: The Stone Benches are situated on flat, even ground and are accessible to all students. However, please note that access to the area may be limited depending on the surrounding landscape and weather conditions.
seating_note: A series of sturdy stone benches provide ample seating. The benches are built into the landscape, offering a rustic and enduring place to sit and enjoy the surroundings.
sense_exp: The Stone Benches are surrounded by an array of interesting plants and greenery due to their adjacency to the Botany department. The natural environment provides a calming and visually stimulating experience. The area is usually quiet, offering a peaceful retreat from the busier parts of the campus.
wayfinding: To find the Stone Benches, head towards the SNIAM building on campus. The benches are located directly in front of the building, adjacent to the Botany department. Look for the stone seating arrangements amidst the lush plant life.
phys_access: The Stone Benches are located on level ground, making them accessible to all students. The area is open and exposed to the elements, so please be mindful of weather conditions that may affect accessibility and comfort.

opening_times.note: This area is outside and is subject to Campus closing times.

name: Iveagh Hall
description: The Entrance Transition Spaces, found near the entrances or stairwells of the Boland Library, are designed to help students adjust to a new sensory environment. These spaces are ideal for pausing to reorient yourself, take a break, or do some casual study before moving on to more focused work in quieter areas of the library. The open design and easy access make these areas versatile, whether you're sitting down for a quick study session or just taking a moment to relax.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: This area is accessible to all students. Positioned near entrances and designed for ease of movement, with wide pathways and plenty of seating options available.
seating_note: The transition spaces offer a variety of seating options to suit different needs. This includes comfortable chairs, high-back seating, and enclosed acoustic seating for those who prefer a little more quiet. Some spaces even have rocking chairs, making it a relaxing place to gather your thoughts or study casually.
sense_exp: This area is well-lit, often benefiting from natural lighting coming through nearby windows. As it is located near busy entrances or stairwells, there is some ambient background noise, but it's generally a calm space that helps ease you into or out of the library environment. The varied seating options also allow students to choose their preferred level of enclosure or openness, depending on their sensory needs.
wayfinding:
You can use the internal library complex navigation tool to find this space and see how to get to it from one of the many entrances to the library complex.

You can find the location of the space within the library [here.](https://app.cloudpano.com/tours/_JKNOIx10eo?sceneId=dn8q4P172d)

name: Botany Court
description: Botany Bay is a historic courtyard, surrounded by student accommodation and features two floodlit all-weather tennis courts and a multi-purpose playing surface that allows for 5-a-side soccer.
wheelchair_note: Access to the gates is via tarmac ramps on both sides.
phys_access:
You must swipe your student or staff card to access the facility. Gates will open automatically once you swipe your student or staff card.

•	Access to the gates is via tarmac ramps on both sides.
•	The court surface is AstroTurf.

opening_times.note: Usage only available through bookings through the Trinity Sport App, sport club, or social activities.

name: Sensory Room
description: This is an enclosed library space with sensory seating and flexible lighting, ideal for studying or resting. It can be used by up to three people at a time, but as it is a library space no talking is permitted. No booking is required for this space.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: This room is accessible
seating_note: There are many different seating options available, between armchairs and rocking chairs.
outlets_note: There are a few sockets available
sense_exp: The room offers a relaxing, quiet break at the centre of the generally busy Arts Building.
wayfinding:
You can use the internal library complex navigation tool to find this space and see how to get to it from one of the many entrances to the library complex.

You can find the location of the space within the library [here](https://app.cloudpano.com/tours/_JKNOIx10eo?sceneId=hcDMDrE3GN).
phys_access: This room is fully accessible

name: Luce Atrium Lower Ground Floor
description: Located just below the ground floor of the Trinity Business School, the basement seating area offers a quieter and more secluded space for students. This area is furnished with a variety of chairs, tables, couches, and vending machines, providing a comfortable environment for relaxation, socialising, or studying. It is conveniently situated next to the bathrooms and is accessible via the main lift, making it easy for all students to reach.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are allowed in this area. Students can bring their own snacks and beverages or use the vending machines available on-site.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: The basement seating area is accessible to all students. To access this area, use the main lift to go downstairs.
seating_note: Seating is available in the form of chairs, tables, and couches. This variety of seating options ensures that students can find a comfortable spot to relax, study, or socialise.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are available, allowing students to charge their devices while using the space.
sense_exp: This area provides a quieter sensory experience compared to the busier ground floor, making it an ideal spot for students seeking a more peaceful environment.
wayfinding:
Enter the business building and walk towards the main reception desk, then turn to the right and follow the staircase down to the open lower level area. Alternatively you can use the main lifts to get down.

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/2JtXDIiPOwE)
phys_access: The area is spacious but tends to be busy and may have many students sitting along the walls or standing in groups.

name: Sensory Rooms
description: The sensory rooms on the second floor of the Eavan Boland Library offer a private, low-distraction environment for quiet, individual study. With four compact, enclosed rooms available, these spaces are perfect for students who need to focus without external disturbances. The rooms are not suitable for taking Zoom or Teams calls, making them ideal for reading, writing, or focused work. Each room is equipped with dimmer switches, allowing students to adjust the lighting levels to their preference.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are not permitted in the sensory rooms to maintain cleanliness and prevent disruptions to the quiet atmosphere.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: Due to the small size of the sensory rooms and narrow hallways to enter them, they may pose a challenge to students using larger mobility aids to make comfortable usage of the rooms.
seating_note: Each sensory room contains one desk and one chair, providing a basic but comfortable setup for individual study. The simplicity of the furnishings contributes to the low-distraction nature of the space, allowing students to concentrate on their work.
outlets_note: There is one power socket available in each room, allowing students to charge their electronic devices while studying.
sense_exp: The sensory rooms are designed to provide a controlled, minimalistic environment. The dimmer switches allow students to adjust the lighting according to their preference, while the enclosed nature of the rooms blocks out external visual distractions. However, because the rooms are small and windowless, some students may find them claustrophobic, though they are perfect for those who thrive in a quiet, distraction-free setting.
wayfinding:
You can use the internal library complex navigation tool to find this space and see how to get to it from one of the many entrances to the library complex.

You can find the location of the space within the library [here.](https://app.cloudpano.com/tours/_JKNOIx10eo?sceneId=wirM90tIQy)

name: House 6 Society Rooms
description: Many Societies have their rooms based in House 6: Fashion, Europa, Dance, Choral, Orchestral, Music, LGBT, PBP, Amnesty, Metafizz, VisArts, Pol Soc, Knitting, Psychology, Gender Equality (DUGES), Literary, SUAS, STAND, Cancer, BioSoc, Environmental, Hiking, DUAMS, Digital Arts DJ, Christian Union, Singers, Comedy, Film, TTV, Trinity FM.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.

opening_times.note: Access to Society Rooms may only be open to Society Members.

name: The Arches Society Rooms
description: The Arches Society Rooms are located within Goldsmith Hall, providing dedicated spaces for a variety of student societies. These rooms are situated deeper within the building, offering a focused environment for different interest groups. Each room is equipped to cater to the specific needs of the societies that use them, supporting a wide range of activities from meetings to events. TAF, Gamers, Sci Fi, Jazz, Trad Soc, Computer Science.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are allowed in the rooms. This feature supports longer meetings and events where refreshments might be necessary.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the Goldsmith SU Café and The Parlour.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the TBSI Zón Mac Léinn.
wheelchair_note: The Arches Society Rooms are accessible to all students.
seating_note: Each room in The Arches is equipped with seating arrangements tailored to its specific use. Options include comfortable chairs for discussions, tables for group work, and flexible seating for events.
outlets_note: The rooms are equipped with power outlets to accommodate electronic devices and equipment needed for society activities.
sense_exp: Each room has its own unique atmosphere depending on its purpose and the activities it supports. The design aims to create a welcoming and functional space for each society’s needs.
wayfinding:
To find The Arches Society Rooms, enter Goldsmith Hall and proceed deeper into the building. Follow the signs or consult a campus map for directions to the specific rooms allocated to each society.

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/-Re-aUur2iA)

opening_times.note: Access to Society Rooms may only be open to Society Members.

name: Academic Registry Quiet Room
description: The Academic Registry Quiet Room, located just off the main Academic Registry, is a sensory-friendly space designed for student respite and individual meetings. This room provides a calm and quiet environment where students can relax, study, or meet with Academic Registry staff to address any queries. Primarily used for individual meetings during September, the Quiet Room is open to all students as a peaceful retreat for the remainder of the year.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and Drink isn't permitted here, the nearest place from here you could eat is the Global Room.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
wheelchair_note: The Academic Registry Quiet Room is fully accessible to students with disabilities. The space is designed with inclusivity in mind, featuring wide entryways and accessible seating areas to accommodate all students.
seating_note: The Quiet Room offers comfortable seating options, including rocking chairs, bean bags, and tables. The layout is designed to provide a relaxing atmosphere conducive to both relaxation and focused work.
outlets_note: Numerous plug sockets are available, ensuring that you can keep your devices charged while using the Quiet Room. Whether you need to power your laptop, tablet, or phone, you’ll find adequate outlets to meet your needs.
sense_exp: The Quiet Room offers a soothing sensory experience with features such as flexible lighting, minimal noise, and comfortable seating. The environment is tailored to reduce sensory overload, making it an ideal place for students seeking a calm and restful space.
wayfinding:
Clear signage is provided throughout the Academic Registry to help you locate the Quiet Room. There is large sign above the door to help, you can also ask for directions at the Academic Registry Service Desk.

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/53aLBPtvAiQ)
phys_access: The Quiet Room provides a tranquil and supportive physical environment. Designed for both relaxation and productivity, the room features ergonomic seating, soft lighting, and a layout that encourages a peaceful atmosphere. The space is maintained to high standards to ensure cleanliness and comfort.

opening_times.note: This area may be in use by Academic Registry Staff for quiet meetings.

name: Entrance Transition Space
description: The Entrance Transition Space offers a relaxed and informal study environment right inside the main entrance of the Lecky Library. This space is ideal for students seeking a less structured setting to work or read. With a variety of comfortable seating options and excellent natural light, it provides a pleasant atmosphere for both focused study and casual browsing. The space is also designed to accommodate ambient background noise, making it a versatile choice for different study preferences.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The Entrance Transition Space is fully accessible, with the Lecky Library providing ramps and lifts for ease of access throughout the building.
seating_note: The Entrance Transition Space features a diverse range of seating to suit different needs, such as Enclosed Acoustic Seating, Rocking Chairs, and Fixed High Back Seating.
sense_exp:
The space benefits from excellent natural light, creating a bright and inviting environment.
The background noise level is moderate, providing a comfortable balance between quiet and ambient sounds, which can be conducive to study.
wayfinding:
You can use the internal library complex navigation tool to find this space and see how to get to it from one of the many entrances to the library complex.

You can find the location of the space within the library [here](https://app.cloudpano.com/tours/_JKNOIx10eo?sceneId=6Xg0lxpfdO).

name: An Mheitheal
description: A large meeting room, with tables, chairs, projectors and a large interactive monitor.   This space provides a quiet meeting or presentation space, with good natural light and is also used for group activities through the Disability Service and College Health Service.
food_drink_allowed_note: Please clean up after yourself using the bins provided, there is also a cold water dispenser in the corner of the room
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6, or The Atrium.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The room is accessible through a lift outside and the side door of the building which acts as the main door for usage
seating_note: There are large numbers of mixed seating available, between chairs, stools, beanbags, and long couches
outlets_note: There are many sockets available in the room, they can be found both along the walls and at the centre of the floor
sense_exp: The room can be divided into 2 smaller rooms to reduce noise levels, otherwise, there tends to be a low humming and occasional noises from the offices and upstairs accommodations. The room can get warm and stuffy if the windows are not open or the air conditioning is turned off. The wall pattern may present an odd visual experience, but this has been mitigated with many things up on the walls.
wayfinding: The most popular door to the room is by going down a staircase, or lift outside the printing house's main square. The door should be open in the case of an event but if closed, it can only be opened with swipe card access, please get in touch with the event host in this situation
phys_access: The room is accessible in all areas

opening_times.note: This area can be booked through the Disability Service.

name: Freeman Library
description: The Freeman Library houses a comprehensive collection of books, journals, and maps, as well as past dissertations and theses from Geography students. Located on the ground floor of the Museum Building, the Freeman Library provides a quiet and conducive environment for both individual and group study. Access to the library is only open to students reading geography.
food_drink_allowed_note: No food or drink is allowed in the Freeman Library to maintain a clean and quiet study environment.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: Unfortunately, the Museum Building, where the Freeman Library is located, is completely physically inaccessible to students who may require accessibility accommodations.
seating_note: The library is equipped with rows of study desks, offering ample seating for students.
outlets_note: There are many plug sockets available, ensuring that you can keep your devices charged while you study.
sense_exp: This space offers a quiet and focused environment, ideal for studying. The library’s atmosphere is typically calm, with minimal noise distractions.
wayfinding: The Freeman Library is located on the ground floor of the Museum Building. Once you enter the building, turn left and head down a few steps until you see a door on the left with Freeman Library on it.
phys_access: While the study space itself is well-equipped and conducive to learning, the Museum Building's lack of accessibility accommodations makes it difficult for all students to utilise this resource.

opening_times.note: This area is only accessible to students reading Geography.

name: Rose Garden
description: This is a small outdoor garden, located close to the Pav and Cricket Pitch while remaining a relatively quiet, peaceful location as it is largely enclosed by flowers and trees. There are several benches for people to sit and relax or enjoy a tea/coffee while reaping the benefits of being out in nature.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring food and drink into the Rose Garden. It is a pleasant spot for enjoying a tea or coffee while soaking in the garden's tranquil atmosphere. Whether you're having a picnic or just taking a break, the garden provides a lovely setting for refreshments.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: There are no pathways, but the grass is flat and even allowing for smooth access to benches and nature.
seating_note: The Rose Garden is equipped with several benches strategically placed throughout the garden. These benches provide comfortable seating for individuals or small groups looking to unwind, enjoy a moment of solitude, or engage in quiet conversation. The seating arrangements are designed to enhance the experience of being surrounded by nature.
sense_exp: The Rose Garden offers a rich sensory experience with its vibrant floral scents and the gentle rustle of leaves. The garden's bright and varied colours, combined with the natural sounds of birds and the gentle hum of nature, create a soothing atmosphere. It is a perfect spot for relaxation and sensory enjoyment.
wayfinding: The Rose Garden is located adjacent to the Museum Building.

opening_times.note: This area is outside and is subject to Campus closing times.

name: Luce Atrium
description: The main concourse seating area in the Trinity Business School is located on the ground floor, immediately to the right as you enter the building. This vibrant and welcoming space features an abundance of tables and colourful seating options, making it an ideal spot for students to relax, socialise, or study. The open and spacious layout creates a dynamic environment that caters to various needs and activities.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are allowed in this area. Students can bring their own meals and beverages, making it a convenient spot to enjoy a snack or a meal between classes.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: The main concourse seating area is accessible to all students.
seating_note: Seating is available with numerous tables and a variety of colourful chairs. This diverse seating arrangement ensures that students can find a comfortable spot whether they are alone or in groups.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are rare in this area, there are more likely to be available sockets in the Basement / Lower Ground Floor Seating Area of this building.
sense_exp: This area offers a vibrant sensory experience with its colourful seating and bustling atmosphere. The open layout allows for natural light to fill the space, creating an inviting environment. The area is often busy which creates a noticeable echo.
wayfinding:
Upon entering the Trinity Business School, turn right to find the main concourse seating area.

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/eOhlQK8YjFI)
phys_access: The area is spacious but tends to be busy and may have many students moving chairs or standing in groups.

name: Group Study Room
description: The Group Study Room provides a quieter and more enclosed environment, equipped with amenities to support collaborative and individual study sessions. This space features pods that offer individual study spaces, ideal for focused work with reduced visual distractions and lower levels of ambient light. Located in a small office setting, the room overlooks a central student walkway, providing ample natural lighting through large windows.
food_drink_allowed_note: Please note that food and drink is not permitted in this space, the nearest place this is permitted would be the JCR Hamilton.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
wheelchair_note: The Group Study Room is accessible to all students. The room features wide entryways and is designed to accommodate wheelchair users comfortably.
seating_note: The Group Study Room is furnished with two roundtables and eight office chairs, accommodating small group discussions or individual study sessions. The seating setup promotes collaborative work and comfortable study conditions.
outlets_note: Multiple plug sockets are available within the Group Study Room, ensuring convenient access to power for laptops, chargers, and other electronic devices.
sense_exp: The Group Study Room offers a conducive sensory experience for studying and collaborative work. With natural lighting from large windows and a layout that minimises auditory distractions, the environment supports concentration and productivity.
wayfinding:
The Group Study Room is visible from just inside the Hamilton Library, proceed to the right-hand corner of the area, the doors and walls into the room are glass so that you can see if it is being used.

[Youtube Video]https://youtu.be/P_095qbWvbY)
phys_access: The Group Study Room provides a physically accessible and comfortable environment. With chairs, spacious roundtables, and a layout that promotes interaction and focused study, the room is designed to enhance the study experience for all students.

name: 1937 Reading Room
description: The 1937 Reading Room is a dedicated postgraduate study building, offering a serene and focused environment for advanced academic work. This quiet library space is filled with an extensive collection of books, catering to a wide range of disciplines. The room is designed to support serious study, with rows of seating arranged to maximise concentration and productivity.
food_drink_allowed_note: To maintain the quiet and clean environment of the library, no food or drink is allowed in the 1937 Reading Room. This policy helps ensure that the space remains conducive to study and free from distractions.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the 1937 Common Room.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the 1937 Common Room.
wheelchair_note: The building only has steps at entrances, therefore making the area physically inaccessible or challenging.
seating_note: The 1937 Reading Room features rows of study desks, providing ample space for individual work. The seating is designed to be comfortable for extended periods, ensuring that postgraduate students can focus on their research and studies without distraction.
outlets_note: The reading room is equipped with numerous plug sockets, conveniently located near the study desks, allowing students to keep their laptops and other electronic devices charged while they work.
sense_exp: The 1937 Reading Room is characterised by its quiet and peaceful atmosphere, ideal for focused study. The presence of rows of books and the general layout contribute to a traditional library environment, where silence is maintained, and distractions are minimal.
phys_access: The 1937 Reading Room is an older building, and while the study area is designed for postgraduate use, students with accessibility needs should note that the building is generally inaccessible.

opening_times.note: This area is only accessible to postgraduate students.

name: ATIC Space Hamilton
description: The Hamilton ATIC (Assistive Technology Information Centres) Space provides a quiet and enclosed environment designed for focused study and work. This small room features flexible seating options, height-adjustable desks, and enclosed desks to minimize distractions. It offers individual study pods ideal for students seeking a serene atmosphere with reduced visual distractions and lower ambient light levels.
food_drink_allowed_note: Please note that food and drink are not permitted in the Hamilton ATIC Space. This policy helps maintain a clean and focused environment for all students using the facility.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
wheelchair_note: The Hamilton ATIC Space is fully accessible to all students. The space is designed with accessibility in mind, featuring wide doorways and ample manoeuvring space.
seating_note: The Hamilton ATIC Space offers flexible seating arrangements to accommodate different study preferences. Whether you prefer a traditional desk setup or a more relaxed seating option, you'll find choices that support comfort and productivity.
outlets_note: Numerous plug sockets are available throughout the Hamilton ATIC Space, ensuring convenient access to power for laptops, chargers, and other electronic devices.
sense_exp: The Hamilton ATIC Space provides a conducive sensory environment for studying and focused work. With adjustable lighting options and a layout that minimises auditory distractions, students can customise their study environment to suit their needs.
wayfinding:
Please see the location here: https://wagnerguide.com/c/trinitycollegedublin/hamiltonlibrary?animation=18796

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/NxpkHjA8Td4)
phys_access: The Hamilton ATIC Space offers a comfortable and productive physical environment. With height-adjustable desks and ergonomic seating options, the space is designed to support long study sessions while minimising physical strain. The layout promotes a focused atmosphere conducive to academic success.

name: 5th Floor Garden
description: The 5th Floor Garden in the Arts Building is a tranquil rooftop garden open to all Trinity staff and students. This enclosed garden features a variety of plants and a few benches, providing a peaceful environment for relaxation and study. While generally quiet, there can be a low droning sound from the building's ventilation system. This space is perfect for those seeking a relaxed place to sit, study, or enjoy lunch, weather permitting.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring your own food and drinks to the 5th Floor Garden. It is an ideal spot to enjoy your lunch in a serene and natural setting.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The garden is accessible to all students. The space is designed to be inclusive, with pathways and seating that accommodate various mobility needs.
seating_note: The garden offers several benches for seating. These benches are strategically placed to provide comfortable spots for relaxation and contemplation amidst the greenery.
outlets_note: There are no sockets available, however, charging spaces can be found just inside on the 5th floor of the Arts Building.
sense_exp: The 5th Floor Garden provides a sensory-rich environment with the natural sounds of rustling leaves and bird calls, complemented by the visual beauty of diverse plant species. The low droning sound from the ventilation system is generally unobtrusive but may be noticeable.
wayfinding: To find the 5th Floor Garden, enter the Arts Building and head to the fifth floor, continue down the hall until you see the windows that show the garden area.
phys_access: The area can be a bit tight to navigate, but is accessible via the main doorway.

name: Atrium Society Rooms
description: The Atrium Society Rooms are a key hub for student societies, providing dedicated spaces for various groups to hold meetings, events, and activities. Located within the Atrium building, these rooms are utilised by a diverse range of societies, each with its own unique focus and interests. List of societies within the Atrium: Fine Gael, Photography, Labour, Mature Students, Sign Language, TES, Geography, Fianna Fail, Food & Drink, Yoga, Cumman Gealach, Law Soc, Cards, Workers Party, History, Classical, ModLang, and Archeology.
food_drink_allowed_note: Most rooms allow for the consumption of food and drink, making them suitable for longer meetings or social events where refreshments are needed
microwave_note: There are two microwaves available on the first floor of the Atrium building. To access them, head up the stairs and through the door located directly above Atrium Room 2. These microwaves are available for use by all those hosting events in the Atrium Rooms.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The Atrium building is wheelchair accessible, with ramps available for entry. However, access to individual rooms is via stairs as there is no lift. The narrow corridors and room layouts may affect movement and sound levels, particularly during busy periods
seating_note: Some society rooms are equipped with flexible seating arrangements to accommodate meetings, discussions, and social events. The rooms can be arranged to suit the specific needs of each society.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are available in each room to support electronic devices and equipment necessary for meetings and events.
sense_exp: The Atrium Society Rooms are designed to cater to a range of sensory preferences. The long and narrow design of the rooms can lead to heightened noise levels during peak times, especially when multiple societies are active simultaneously. The building features natural lighting and a neutral decor that aims to create a conducive environment for both work and social interactions.
wayfinding: To access the Atrium Society Rooms, enter the Atrium building and navigate to the designated rooms. Each room is clearly marked, with directions provided to assist in locating specific societies. For access to the kitchen, head to the first floor, where microwaves and other amenities are available.

name: D'Olier Street Zón Mac Léinn
description: The D'Olier Street Zón Mac Léinn offers a welcoming social space for students, located near the entrance to the School of Nursing and Midwifery. This area provides a variety of seating options, including chairs, tables, couches, and a kitchenette for convenience.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are allowed in this area. Occasionally, there is a small café operating within the space, offering additional refreshments. The kitchenette is equipped with a microwave and a kettle for your convenience.
microwave_note: This area has microwaves.
kettle_note: There is a kettle located in this space.
wheelchair_note: This area is accessible to all students. However, it can become crowded at times, which might make navigation a bit challenging.
seating_note: There are many seating options available, catering to different needs and preferences. Whether you're looking for a comfortable spot to relax or a table to work at, you'll find suitable seating here.
outlets_note: A few plug sockets are available throughout the space, allowing you to charge your devices while you relax or study.
sense_exp: This space can be bustling during peak times, but the variety of seating options helps to create pockets of quieter areas.
wayfinding: This Zón Mac Léinn is situated at the entrance of the School of Nursing and Midwifery which is just off campus on D'Olier Street. The building has large old signage reading "GAS" just above the doorway.
phys_access: The area is fully accessible to all students. The layout is designed to ensure ease of movement, but it may become a bit more difficult to navigate when crowded. All facilities, including the kitchenette and seating areas, are designed to be inclusive.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)

name: Pharmacy Mezzanine
description: The Pharmacy Mezzanine Social Space is a welcoming area located within the Hamilton Building, designed to provide students with a comfortable place to relax, study, or socialise. This space is furnished with a variety of seating options, including sofas and soft stools, and is equipped with several coffee tables, making it ideal for group discussions, casual meetings, or individual study sessions. The area benefits from natural, bright lighting, creating a pleasant and airy atmosphere. Additionally, students can find a Trinity Publications shelf, offering a range of reading materials for those interested.
food_drink_allowed_note: Feel free to bring your food and beverages as this space is designed to be a flexible area where you can enjoy your meals and snacks while socialising or relaxing.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: This space is fully accessible to students. The space is designed with inclusivity in mind, featuring an open-plan layout and easily accessible seating areas to accommodate wheelchairs.
seating_note: The social space offers a total of six sofas, providing ample seating for students. These are complemented by soft stools and five coffee tables, ensuring there’s plenty of space to sit comfortably, whether you’re working on a project or taking a break with friends.
outlets_note: Numerous plug sockets are available, ensuring you can charge your devices while you relax. They can be found in the far corners behind the couches.
sense_exp: This space provides a vibrant yet comfortable environment, balancing lively social interactions with an area for quieter relaxation. Soft natural lighting, comfortable seating, and usually decent temperatures cater to different sensory preferences. The atmosphere is dynamic, making it a great place to recharge and connect with fellow students.
wayfinding:
This space can be found above the security hut in the East End of the Hamilton Building. There is a staircase leading up to it. There is a lift that can bring you to the right floor of the Panoz to access this space, found in the middle of the main hall area.

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/-OObLO7tqAo)
phys_access: The layout encourages social interaction while also providing nooks for individual relaxation. The space is well-maintained, clean, and conducive to both socialising and resting.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)
aka: Panoz Zón Mac Léinn, ZML Panoz

name: 2nd Floor Seating, Arts Building
description: The 2nd Floor Seating Area in the Arts Building offers a variety of casual seating options along a long hallway. This space features chairs, couches, benches, and seating pods, providing comfortable spots for relaxation and socializing. Due to its location near several large lecture theatres, the area experiences significant foot traffic, making it a bustling hub for students between classes.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are accessible, with vending machines and nearby cafes providing refreshments. You can enjoy a snack or a drink in the seating area while taking a break from your studies.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The seating area is accessible to all students. The layout ensures easy navigation and access for everyone, including those with mobility needs. The study pods however may not be fully accessible depending on their design.
seating_note: Various forms of casual seating are available along the hallway, including soft benches, comfortable couches, and individual seating pods. These options cater to different needs, whether you're looking to relax, study, or chat with friends.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are available throughout the area, allowing students to charge their devices conveniently while they study or relax.
sense_exp: The sensory experience in this area includes the lively atmosphere of student interactions and ambient noise from the foot traffic. While it can be crowded, the various seating options provide a comfortable space to unwind or study.
wayfinding: The "2nd Floor" is often confused with the Ground Floor of the Arts Building, when you enter via Nassau St. or Fellow's Square this hallway area consists of most of 2nd floor of the building between lecture theatres.
phys_access: The area is accessible to all students, with clear pathways and accessible seating arrangements. The design ensures that all students can navigate the space comfortably, with consideration for those with mobility needs.

name: The Perch
description: The Perch is a popular café located within the Arts Building right at the main entrance from Fellows' Square. This vibrant spot serves a variety of beverages including coffee, tea, hot chocolate, and cold drinks, along with a selection of snacks. It's a favourite among students for a quick pick-me-up between lectures or a place to unwind with friends.
food_drink_allowed_note: The Perch offers a range of food and drink options that can be enjoyed within the café space or in the surrounding seating areas. Students are welcome to purchase items on-site and savour them wherever they find a comfortable spot.
wheelchair_note: The Perch and its surrounding seating areas are fully accessible to all students. The Arts Building is equipped with accessible entrances and pathways, ensuring that students using wheelchairs or those with other mobility needs can easily navigate the space and enjoy the café.
seating_note: While The Perch itself is a small café space, it benefits from ample seating options available throughout the surrounding Arts Building. There are plenty of spots to sit inside, or you can choose to enjoy your drink just outside the entrance, taking in the fresh air and the bustling campus atmosphere.
outlets_note: The seating areas around The Perch, both inside the Arts Building and near the entrance, are equipped with plug sockets. This makes it convenient for students who want to charge their devices while they relax with a drink.
sense_exp:
The Perch is a lively café with a constant flow of students, especially during peak hours. The atmosphere is energised by the aroma of freshly brewed coffee and the chatter of students passing through. 

With its location at the main entrance, the café captures the dynamic spirit of campus life, making it an ideal spot for those who thrive in a bustling environment.
wayfinding: The Perch is located at the main entrance of the Arts Building, facing Fellows' Square. It’s easy to find, as it’s one of the first things you’ll see when entering from this side of the campus. Clear signage within the Arts Building also points towards the café.

opening_times.note: Open until 6pm on Fridays

name: Montgomery
description:
On the ground floor. A former lecture room, now a student and staff social space, to eat lunch or sit down and relax. (Microwaves coming soon!)

There are more facilities coming to this room in the coming year
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are allowed
microwave_note: Microwaves coming soon!
wheelchair_note: Room has level access and is on ground floor. Room has space for wheelchair users to move around, but as furniture is not fixed there may be obstructions at times to parts of the room.
seating_note: There is seating available mostly chairs and tables with some sofas
outlets_note: There are sockets
sense_exp: Can be loud when busy at peak lunch times. Old lecture room with overhead lighting and windows.
wayfinding: From the main entrance, past reception through the double doors on the right, continue down the hallway and through another set of double doors, entrance to the montgomery lecture hall is to your left.
phys_access: Hallways are quite wide, with sets of push double doors.

name: AAP Café
description: The Aras an Phiarsaigh (AAP) Café is a cosy and quiet café located at the entrance of the Aras an Phiarsaigh building. This small, relaxed space offers a coffee dock, vending machines, and several tables with seating. It's an ideal spot for students to unwind, grab a quick coffee, or enjoy a light snack between classes.
food_drink_allowed_note: The café offers a variety of light food and drink options. The coffee dock serves freshly brewed coffee and tea, while the vending machines provide a selection of snacks and beverages. This makes it easy to grab a quick refreshment without having to leave the building.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the Atrium or the SU Kitchen, House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The café is accessible to all students, ensuring that all students can enjoy the space comfortably. The entrance and seating arrangements are designed to accommodate.
seating_note: Seating is available throughout the café, with several tables and chairs arranged to accommodate both individual visitors and small groups. The layout is designed to promote a comfortable and casual atmosphere, perfect for study breaks or socialising with friends.
outlets_note: A few plug sockets are available in the café, allowing you to charge your devices while you relax. Whether you need to power your laptop for some quick work or charge your phone, you'll find convenient access to power outlets.
sense_exp: The café provides a calm sensory experience with soft lighting and a generally quiet atmosphere. The presence of a coffee dock adds a pleasant aroma of freshly brewed coffee, contributing to a cosy and inviting environment
wayfinding: Just inside on the left when you enter the Aras an Phiarsaigh building.
phys_access: The area is easily navigated, and furniture can be easily moved to accommodate table usage. While the coffee dock counter might be too tall for usage, the attendants are easily able to move around to serve any beverages from it. Some vending machine operation panels could be just a little out-of-reach to some people.

name: Cricket Pitch Benches (East)
description: The Cricket Pitch Benches on the east side of the pitch offer a serene outdoor seating area along the large grass area of the campus. These benches provide a peaceful place to relax and enjoy the outdoors, with a view of the cricket pitch. Located adjacent to The Pavillion Bar, the benches can become busier and more social in the evenings and during large events.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are available nearby at The Pavillion Bar (The Pav). This convenient proximity allows students to enjoy refreshments in the outdoor seating area.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: The Cricket Pitch Benches area is accessible to all students. The paths leading to the benches are well-maintained to ensure ease of access for everyone.
seating_note: Seating is available with several benches running alongside the cricket pitch. These benches offer a great spot for relaxation, socialising, or simply enjoying the view of the green space.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are unavailable in this outdoor space. Students needing to charge their devices should plan accordingly.
sense_exp: This area provides a pleasant sensory experience with the natural ambience of the cricket pitch and the surrounding greenery. While generally peaceful during the day, it can become lively and bustling in the evenings, especially during events at The Pav.

opening_times.note: This area is outside and is subject to Campus closing times.

name: Seomra na Gaeilge
