description:
Spás geal compordach caidrimh agus comhrá do lucht na Gaeilge sa Choláiste atá ann. Bíonn leabhair, foilseacháin agus cluichí cláir/cártaí i nGaeilge ar fáil sa seomra. Tá go leor cathaoireacha compordacha uilline sa seomra, chomh maith le táblaí atá oiriúnach don ithe, do chruinnithe, agus d’imirt cluichí boird/cártaí. Sa chistin bheag tá áiseanna tae agus caife, doirteal agus micrea-oigheann. Iarratar deonachán beag 20c do na sólaistí.
||
A bright, comfortable space for the Irish-speaking community of the College to mix and chat. There are Irish-language books, publications and board games/cards available in the room. The room is furnished with many comfortable armchairs, as well as tables suitable for eating, for meetings, and for playing board games/cards. The kitchenette has facilities for tea and coffee, a sink and microwave.
food_drink_allowed_note:
Tá fáilte roimh mhic léinn bia a ithe agus deochanna neamh-mheisciúla a ól i Seomra na Gaeilge. Ní féidir bia a cheannach anseo, agus tá uisce as an sconna ar fáil.
Students are welcome to consume food and non-alcoholic drinks in Seomra na Gaeilge. Food cannot be bought here, and tap water is available.
microwave_note:
Tá micrea-oigheann amháin sa Seomra.
Seomra na Gaeilge has one microwave.
kettle_note:
Níl aon chiteal sa seomra ach tá uisce te ar fáil ón dáileoir uisce te.
There is no kettle in the room but hot water is available from the hot water dispenser.
wheelchair_note:
Níl Seomra na Gaeilge inrochtana ag cathaoireacha rothaí faoi láthair.
Seomra na Gaeilge is not currently wheelchair accessible.
seating_note:
28 cathaoir uillinne íseal stuáilte - 28 low, cushioned armchairs
4 stólta arda ag cuntar na cistine - 4 high stools at the kitchenette counter
8 cathaoir staidéir stuáilte - 8 cushioned study chairs
outlets_note:
Tá trí shoicéad balla ar fáil gar do na doirse i ngach cúinne sa Seomra (seachas an cúinne ina bhfuil an chistin bheag).
There are three wall sockets available near the doors in each corner of the room (except the corner where the kitchenette is)
sense_exp:
Solas: Solas nádúrtha a bhíonn i Seomra na Gaeilge den chuid is mó, go háirithe ó na fuinneoga móra ar an taobh thoir.
Lighting: Seomra na Gaeilge is mostly filled with natural light, especially from the large windows on its east-facing side.
Fuaim: Bíonn an fhuaim íseal go leor sa Seomra go hiondúil. Cairpéad atá ar an gcuid is mó den urlár, a sheachnaíonn fuaim ard ó choischéimeanna agus bogadh troscáin. Ní bhíonn torann ó taobh amuigh seachas má bhíonn fuaim ard ag teacht ó na cúirteanna leadóige. Mar gur áit shóisialta í seo, is féidir leis an bhfuaim a bheith ard ag brath ar líon na ndaoine atá istigh ann. Ní bhíonn raidió ná ceol ar siúl sa Seomra mura dtagann sé ó úsáideoirí an tSeomra iad féin.
Noise: Sound levels in the room tend to be generally quite low. The floor is mostly carpet which avoids noise from footsteps or moving furniture. There is very little noise from outside unless there is loud noise coming from the tennis courts. Since this is a social space, noise levels may be high depending on the number of people in the room. There is no radio or music played unless it comes from the users of the room themselves.
wayfinding:
Tá an Seomra lonnaithe i bhfoirgneamh an Phroinntí, os cionn bialann an Bhutraigh, ar an dara hurlár. Téann tú isteach trí dhoras taobh thiar den Bhutrach, seach na cúirteanna leadóige i mBá na Luibheolaíochta, agus suas ansin go barr an staighre.
The Room is located in the Dining Hall building, over the Buttery restaurant, on the second floor. Please go around the right hand side of the Buttery on the outside (past the tennis courts on Botany Bay) and enter through the wooden rear door at the back of the building. Go up the stairs to the very top.
phys_access:
Caithfear dul síos staighre agus suas staighre le teacht ar an seomra. Níl ardaitheoir ar fáil faoi láthair le teacht go Seomra na Gaeilge.
You have to go both downstairs and upstairs to reach the room. There is currently no elevator access to Seomra na Gaeilge
further_info:
Is féidir iarratas a dhéanamh chun imeacht a chur ar siúl i Seomra na Gaeilge. Tuilleadh eolais ag https://www.tcd.ie/gaeloifig/seomra-gaeilge/

You can make a request to hold an event in Seomra na Gaeilge. More information here: https://www.tcd.ie/gaeloifig/seomra-gaeilge/

opening_times.note: Is féidir iarratas a dhéanamh chun imeacht a chur ar siúl i Seomra na Gaeilge. Tuilleadh eolais ag... || You can make a request to hold an event in Seomra na Gaeilge. More information here: https://www.tcd.ie/gaeloifig/seomra-gaeilge/

name: JCR Hamilton
description: The JCR Hamilton Zón Mac Léinn, is an ideal social space for students to relax, have lunch, and socialize. Equipped with microwaves, a fridge, and a kettle, this space is perfect for preparing and enjoying meals. Offering a variety of seating options suitable for both groups and individuals. Additionally, there are individual rooms downstairs equipped with desks and chairs, providing a quiet environment for studying, working on assignments, or attending remote classes.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring your own food and drinks to the JCR Hamilton. The space is equipped with microwaves for heating meals, a sink to washup, and a kettle for hot beverages. These facilities make it easy to prepare and enjoy your meals in a comfortable setting.
microwave_note: There are microwaves are available in the JCR Hamilton, allowing you to heat up your meals and enjoy hot food during your time in the space.
kettle_note: A kettle is available in the JCR Hamilton for students to use, making it convenient to prepare hot drinks like tea or coffee.
wheelchair_note: The JCR Hamilton is wheelchair accessible at the ground floor level. The space is designed to accommodate all students, featuring wide entryways and accessible seating areas. However, please note that access to the downstairs individual rooms may be limited.
seating_note: The JCR Hamilton provides numerous seating options to accommodate different needs and preferences. Whether you're looking to sit with a group of friends or prefer a more solitary setup, you'll find comfortable chairs, sofas, and tables designed to create a welcoming and flexible environment.
outlets_note: Multiple plug sockets are available throughout the JCR Hamilton, ensuring you can easily charge your electronic devices. Whether you're working on your laptop, attending remote classes, or charging your phone, you'll find convenient access to power outlets.
sense_exp: This space provides a dynamic sensory experience, balancing lively social interactions with quieter areas for individual study. The environment is designed to cater to different sensory preferences, with spaces that offer both bustling activity and calm retreat.
wayfinding: The doors to the JCR Hamilton can be found on the outside of the Hamilton Building, near the Student Union Shop.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)

name: Buttery Vaults
description: The Buttery Vaults is a designated Zón Mac Léinn located next to the main Buttery restaurant. This space provides a comfortable and convenient area for students to relax, socialise, or study, with ample seating and tables available.
food_drink_allowed_note: Outside food and drink are allowed in the Buttery Vaults. Additionally, you can purchase food and drinks from the Buttery kitchen as well as the coffee station, making it a versatile spot for dining and studying.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the Atrium.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: This area is accessible to all students. However, when crowded, it might pose a challenge to navigate. The layout is designed to be inclusive, but the high traffic during peak times can make movement a bit more difficult.
seating_note: There are a variety of seating options available, including chairs and tables, as well as cushioned stools and couches along the walls. This mix of seating types ensures that students can find a spot that suits their needs, whether they're working on assignments or catching up with friends.
outlets_note: There are a few plug sockets available, though they are sparsely located along the walls. It's advisable to charge your devices beforehand if you plan to spend an extended period here.
sense_exp: The Buttery Vaults are connected to the main Buttery restaurant, which tends to be noisy and crowded during peak lunchtime hours. However, this room can act as a buffer, reducing some of the noise and smells from the kitchen. It's a good spot if you want to be close to the action but still need a bit of a break from the busiest areas.
wayfinding:
There are several entrances to the Vaults:

- Two entrances from the Buttery restaurant
- One entrance from the hallways under the dining complex
- Another door that tends to be locked leading to the Atrium main hall
phys_access: The Buttery Vaults are fully accessible to all students. The area is designed with inclusivity in mind, though it can become crowded at times, which might make navigation slightly more challenging.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)

opening_times.note: This area can be booked in the evenings through the SU.

name: 1st Floor Seating, Arts Building
description: The seating areas in the Arts Building's 1st Floor offer a variety of seating options, including tables, chairs, couches, and benches. Conveniently located close to The Perch, a popular student coffee and refreshment shop, this area is situated outside one of the largest lecture theatres on campus. It is an ideal spot for students to relax, study, or socialise between classes. While the area tends to be lively and can get quite loud, it remains a favoured space for many due to its central location and accessibility.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are readily available, with The Perch café located just steps away. You can enjoy a coffee, snack, or meal in the seating area, making it a perfect spot for a break between lectures.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The seating area is designed to be accessible to all students. The layout ensures easy movement and access for everyone, including those with mobility needs.
seating_note: Seating is plentiful and diverse, with options ranging from individual chairs and tables to couches and benches. Whether you're looking to study alone, work in a group, or just relax, you'll find a seating arrangement that suits your needs.
outlets_note: Numerous plug sockets are available throughout the area, making it convenient for students to charge their laptops, phones, and other electronic devices while they work or relax.
sense_exp: The sensory experience in this area includes natural light from nearby windows and the ambient sounds of student activity. While it can become noisy due to the high volume of people, it remains a comfortable and engaging space for social interaction and study.
wayfinding: From the main entrances of the Arts Block, near the Perch café, turn right and go down the steps until you see an area of red-coloured circular couches and tables.
phys_access: The area is fully accessible. The lift adjacent The Perch will be needed to access this area.

name: Business School Courtyard
description: The Business School Courtyard is a tranquil outdoor area adjacent to the Forum Café. This courtyard provides a serene environment for students and staff to relax, socialise, or enjoy a meal outdoors. With ample seating options and natural greenery, it is a perfect spot to take a break between lectures or meetings.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are allowed in the courtyard. Students and staff can bring their own meals or purchase refreshments from the nearby Forum Café.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: The Business School Courtyard is accessible to all students. The layout is designed to be inclusive, with pathways and seating arrangements that cater to everyone.
seating_note: Seating is available throughout the courtyard, offering a variety of options including benches and tables to accommodate both individuals and groups.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are unavailable in this outdoor space, so it is recommended to charge your devices beforehand if you plan to work or study here.
sense_exp: This courtyard offers a pleasant sensory experience with its natural surroundings and the gentle hum of activity from the nearby café. The space is generally peaceful, making it a good spot for relaxation and informal gatherings.
wayfinding: Upon exiting the Trinity Business School turn left and walk towards the Forum Café.
phys_access: The Courtyard is fully accessible. Pathways are wide and even, and seating areas are designed to accommodate all students. There are no steps or barriers, ensuring easy navigation for everyone.

name: Wild Garden
description: The Wild Gardens is a delightful natural retreat located on campus, designed to celebrate the untamed beauty of the outdoors. This garden area is surrounded by lush, native plant growth and features an array of bird and animal feeders, making it a haven for local wildlife. At the centre of the garden, you will find two benches, strategically placed to offer a peaceful vantage point for observing the vibrant natural surroundings.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring food and drink into the Wild Gardens. The serene environment is ideal for a relaxed picnic or a quiet coffee break while enjoying the view of the garden's natural beauty. Please ensure that you clean up after yourself to help maintain the garden's pristine condition.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: The Wild Gardens is accessible to all students. The paths within the garden are designed to accommodate wheelchairs and other mobility aids, ensuring easy access to the benches and various parts of the garden. The layout allows for smooth navigation throughout the space.
seating_note: The Wild Gardens features two benches situated at the heart of the garden. These benches are positioned to provide a comfortable and serene place to sit and enjoy the natural scenery. Whether you're taking a break, reading a book, or simply soaking in the tranquillity, the benches offer a perfect spot to connect with nature.
sense_exp: The Wild Gardens offers a rich sensory experience with its vibrant natural surroundings. The sound of birds chirping and the sight of diverse wildlife create a calming atmosphere. The garden's varied textures and scents from the native plants add to the immersive experience, making it a refreshing spot for relaxation and observation.
wayfinding: Found between the cricket and rugby pitches.

opening_times.note: This area is outside and is subject to Campus closing times.

name: Cricket Pitch Benches (West)
description: The Cricket Pitch Benches (West) are a series of benches that run alongside the cricket pitch near the Libraries and Arts Building. This area is characterized by its tranquillity and quieter atmosphere compared to other parts of the pitch. The benches are shaded and covered by large trees, offering a peaceful outdoor seating option ideal for relaxation and studying.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are accessible nearby. The Pavillion Bar (The Pav) and other campus cafes offer refreshments that can be enjoyed while sitting on the benches.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The Cricket Pitch Benches (West) area is accessible to all students. The pathways leading to the benches are well-maintained to ensure ease of access for everyone.
seating_note: Seating is available with several benches positioned along the cricket pitch. These benches provide a serene spot to sit and enjoy the shaded surroundings.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are unavailable in this outdoor space. Students needing to charge their devices should plan accordingly.
sense_exp: This area offers a peaceful sensory experience, with the shade and cover provided by large trees creating a calming atmosphere. It is quieter than other parts of the cricket pitch, making it an ideal spot for students seeking a tranquil outdoor study or relaxation space.

opening_times.note: This area is outside and is subject to Campus closing times.

name: Cricket Pitch Benches
description: The Cricket Pitch Benches are a series of benches that run alongside the cricket pitch, which is also the main grassy area of the campus. These benches offer a comfortable outdoor seating area perfect for relaxation, socialising, or enjoying a meal. Due to their location along one of the main pathways connecting the east and west ends of the campus, this area tends to be busy with students, staff, and tourists, particularly during good weather.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are accessible nearby. The Pavillion Bar (The Pav) and other campus cafes offer refreshments that can be enjoyed while sitting on the benches.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The Cricket Pitch Benches (Main) area is accessible to all students. The pathways leading to the benches are well-maintained to ensure ease of access for everyone.
seating_note: Seating is available with numerous benches running along the cricket pitch. These benches provide an excellent spot to sit and relax while enjoying the view of the campus's large grassy area.
outlets_note: Plug sockets are unavailable in this outdoor space. Students needing to charge their devices should plan accordingly.
sense_exp: This area offers a vibrant sensory experience, with the natural ambiance of the cricket pitch and the surrounding greenery. While it can be peaceful, the proximity to the main pathway means it is often lively and bustling with foot traffic, especially during pleasant weather.

opening_times.note: This area is outside and is subject to Campus closing times.

name: Seating Pods
description: Discover the two sensory pods situated on the ground floor of the Hamilton Building, located conveniently in the main hallways. These pods are designed to offer a calming and focused environment for students seeking a calm study area, or social space. There is also a monitor available.
food_drink_allowed_note: Feel free to bring along your snacks and beverages. The Hamilton Building encourages a study-friendly environment where you can keep hydrated and energised with your own food and drink.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here would be in the Hamilton JCR.
wheelchair_note: The sensory pods are not fully wheelchair accessible.
seating_note: The sensory pods come equipped with comfortable bench seating arrangements to ensure a pleasant and ergonomic study experience. Whether you're here for a quick review session or an extended study period, the seating is designed to support your posture and minimise discomfort.
outlets_note: Each sensory pod is fitted with multiple plug sockets, allowing you to charge your devices easily. Whether you need to power up your laptop, phone, or tablet, you'll find sufficient outlets to keep your devices running throughout your study session.
sense_exp: The sensory pods are designed to provide a serene and distraction-free study environment. With features such as noise reduction panels, adjustable lighting, and comfortable seating, these pods aim to enhance focus and reduce sensory overload. Whether you prefer dim lighting or a brighter setting, you can customise your pod to suit your preferences.
wayfinding:
The pods can be located on the ground floor next to the Biology and Chemistry Labs, at the end of the Hamilton Building.

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/qSAQx_Lsqz4)

name: Room 4017
description:
Room 4017 is a vibrant and inviting Student Zone (Zón Mac Léinn) designed for relaxation and socialising. Located within a large academic building, this space features a colourful carpet, diverse furniture options, and numerous tables and seating arrangements. It's an ideal spot for eating lunch, chatting with friends, or taking a break between lectures. Additionally, it offers ample charging points, making it suitable for studying or working on assignments. However, due to its popularity, the room can get busy and noisy during peak times, particularly around lunchtime.
[WC] There are gendered, gender-neutral and accessible toilets accessible on same floor
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring your food and drinks. It's a perfect spot to enjoy a meal or a snack in between classes, and the room's amenities support a relaxed dining experience.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The room is fully accessible to all students. The space is designed with inclusivity in mind, featuring wide entryways and accessible seating arrangements to ensure comfort and ease of movement for all students.
seating_note: The Arts Block Social Space is equipped with seven comfortable sofas, providing ample seating for students. The seating is arranged around small, shin-height tables, making it a suitable spot for casual conversations, group work, or simply unwinding between lectures.
outlets_note: Multiple plug sockets are available throughout, providing convenient access to power for laptops, chargers, and other electronic devices. This makes it easy to stay productive while enjoying the social space.
sense_exp: The space provides a lively sensory environment with its colourful decor and dynamic layout. While it offers a vibrant atmosphere, students should be aware that it can become noisy and bustling during peak times, particularly around lunchtime.
wayfinding: To find Room 4017, enter the academic building and follow the signs directing you to the fourth floor. Once on the fourth floor, look for signage indicating Room 4017. You can also ask for directions at the main reception desk.
phys_access: The Arts Block Social Space is located in a building that is wheelchair accessible, with both lift and stair access. The floors are carpeted, providing a smooth and comfortable surface for movement. However, the doorways into the social space itself may be challenging to navigate due to the push/pull system. While the area is otherwise accessible, this feature might pose difficulties for some students. Toilets on the same floor include gendered, gender-neutral, and accessible options, ensuring that all students have access to appropriate facilities.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)

name: Printing House Square – Sport
description:
At Printing House Square, you’ll find three dynamic squash courts, a GAA handball alley, and a cutting-edge Olympic Target range. There is also a viewing area and seating available.
All facilities can be accessed through the door beside Aras an Phiarsaigh.
wheelchair_note: The sporting facilities are easily accessible via lift.
seating_note: There is seating available within specific sporting facilities
phys_access:
You must swipe your student or staff card to access the facility. Gates will open automatically once you swipe your student or staff card.
•	There is a lift providing access to the courts, rifle range, changing rooms, and toilets.
•	Inclusive and accessible toilets and changing rooms are available.
•	The facility has both automatic and manual doors.

opening_times.note: Usage only available through bookings through the Trinity Sport App, sport club, or social activities.

name: Rugby Pitch
description: Trinity College Dublin's rugby pitch is part of the historic College Park, a significant green space used for various outdoor sports and recreational activities and the home of the Trinity Rugby Club.
phys_access:
There are barriers that surround the entirety of the pitch with gaps at both ends of the pitch to enter. 
There is tarmac on two sides, a foot path at one end and bark mulch at the other end. 
There is a carpark behind the pitch, which includes designated wheelchair parking spaces.
Bathrooms and refreshments are available close by in the Pavilion Bar.

opening_times.note: Usage only available through bookings through the Trinity Sport App, sport club, or social activities.

name: Common Room
description: The kitchen in the 1937 Reading Room is a welcoming space designed for postgraduate students to eat, socialise, and relax. This cosy area features a variety of seating options, including couches, tables, chairs, and high stools, catering to different preferences and needs. The space is equipped with a microwave and kettle, allowing students to prepare simple meals or hot drinks while taking a break from their studies. The kitchen can accommodate up to 15 people at a time, and its layout, divided by arches, creates smaller, more intimate spaces within the room.
food_drink_allowed_note: As a designated eating area, students are encouraged to bring their own food and drink. The kitchen is equipped with a microwave and kettle, so you can easily heat up your meals or prepare a cup of tea or coffee.
microwave_note: There are microwaves are available, allowing you to heat up your meals and enjoy hot food during your time in this space.
kettle_note: A kettle is available for students to use, making it convenient to prepare hot drinks like tea or coffee.
wheelchair_note: The building only has steps at entrances, therefore making the area physically inaccessible or challenging.
seating_note: The kitchen offers a mix of seating arrangements, with comfortable couches for lounging, tables and chairs for dining or group discussions, and high stools for a more casual seating option. The varied seating options make it easy to find a spot that suits your needs, whether you’re looking to eat, chat with fellow postgraduates, or simply unwind.
outlets_note: There are several plug sockets available in the kitchen area, making it convenient for students to charge their devices while they relax or work.
sense_exp: The kitchen area in the 1937 Reading Room is generally a quiet space, making it suitable for relaxing between study sessions. The division of the room by arches helps to create smaller, more private spaces, enhancing the sense of calm. As an eating area, the space may have some food aromas, adding to the homely atmosphere.
wayfinding: I wonder
phys_access:
The 1937 Reading Room is an older building, and while the kitchen area is designed for postgraduate use, students with accessibility needs should note that the building is generally inaccessible. 
The kitchen’s layout, with arches dividing the space, is designed to create a comfortable environment for those who can navigate the space.

opening_times.note: This area is only accessible to postgraduate students.

name: Hist Conversation Room
description: A large room with tables, chairs, couches and armchairs with a capacity of 80, historically used for Hist members to socialising or work in and hold debates. Societies also book this space to hold socials events, speaker events, or launches for publications. The space is not wheelchair accessible, it is on the first floor of the GMB
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and Drink are allowed to be consumed in this area, there are no facilities for food/drink
wheelchair_note: Not wheelchair accessible - on the first floor
seating_note: There are movable chairs, tables and couches available.
outlets_note: There are three plug sockets along the walls of the room.
sense_exp: There are high windows, which allow a lot of light into the room. There are high ceilings, and the floor is wooden, which means there can often be echoes in the room. The windows open onto Front Square so there is often a low level of background noise.
wayfinding: Walk up the main staircase and take the first door on your left immediately after reaching the first floor landing.
phys_access: The room is large and not cluttered but there are tables both low and high and sofas and chairs which will be re-shuffled and moved across the floor depending on what events the room is being used for that day.

opening_times.note: This space is accessible to all students. For events, this space can be booked by societies and external guests using the GMB Jotform available on the CSC website, subject to Hist, Phil, and Enquiries approval

name: Arts Building Respite Room
description:
This space provides comfortable furniture and flexible lighting to allow students to rest and recuperate. If you’ve had a busy day of lectures, or just need a break from an overwhelming sensory environment, this can be a good place to relax for an hour. The room must be booked in advance of being used as it can only be used by one person at a time. 

The Arts Building Respite Space is managed by the Disability Service and is provided only to students who have applied for supports with the DS. Only those who have been specifically referred for respite by their Disability Officer can access this room. Your student card needs to be activated on referral from your Disability Officer.

Entry to Room 2032 in the Arts Building is by student card access only and must be booked in advance of use. Students are limited to 1 booking per day to ensure availability for other students. Room 2032 can be booked through the Online Booking Calendar only.
food_drink_allowed_note: Students are encouraged to clean up after themselves and avoid bringing food with strong smells into the room to maintain a pleasant environment for everyone. While there is a kettle, tap, and sink available for making tea or coffee, the nearest microwave can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: There is a kettle with a tap and sink available for water
wheelchair_note: The room is fully accessible in all areas, with an assisted door to facilitate easy entry.
seating_note: The room offers a variety of seating options to accommodate different needs, including couches, a bed, and a rocking chair. This variety ensures that students can find the most comfortable position for rest and relaxation.
outlets_note: There are multiple plug sockets available throughout the room, allowing you to charge devices or use electronics as needed during your time in the space.
sense_exp:
This room is designed to be a quiet and calming space, with its deep location within the Arts Building ensuring a high degree of sound insulation. The flexible lighting and comfortable seating options contribute to a soothing environment, ideal for rest and recovery.

Some traffic noise from Nassau Street may occasionally be heard.
wayfinding: The space is positioned on the 2nd floor, close to the building’s accessibility lift. To find the room, walk past the security hut and continue until you see the door on the right.
further_info:
For more details about the Respite Space and how to access it, please refer to the Disability Service’s Respite Space [Information & Booking Page](https://www.tcd.ie/disability/support-and-resources/respite-space/). 

If you have any questions or require assistance with booking, please contact your Disability Officer directly or the Disability Service at askds@tcd.ie.

opening_times.note: This area can be booked through the Disability Service Booking Link.

name: Recreation Room
description: This is a large room with low black couches, a snooker table, some storage cabinets, and a few large tables. There are large windows on one side facing Botany Bay, and two doors.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and Drink are allowed to be consumed in this area, there are no facilities for food/drink.
wheelchair_note: This space is not wheelchair accessible
seating_note: There are low backed couches and a small number of chairs.
outlets_note: There are 4 plug sockets close to the ground in the corners of the room.
sense_exp: This room has large open windows which open onto the tennis courts, meaning a low level of street noise and a lot of natural light during the day. The room has high ceilings and wooden floors meaning there can be echoes.
wayfinding: Walk up the main staircase in the GMB to the second floor, go through the double doors on your left at the end of the landing, and then go through the door immediately to your right.
phys_access: There is little clutter but couches and tables of varying height. There is a large snooker table that takes the center of the room; the doors are large and can be heavy.

opening_times.note: This space is accessible to all students. Societies can book it for events using the GMB Jotform on the CSC website.

name: Sports Centre Respite Room
description:
This is a space for students who regularly experience pain or fatigue as a result of a disability, and must be booked in advance of being used. It can only be used by one person at a time, and it provides comfortable furniture and flexible lighting to allow students to rest and recuperate. If you’ve had a busy day of lectures, or just need a break from an overwhelming sensory environment, this can be a good place to relax for an hour. 

The respite room in the Sports Centre is available for booking Mondays to Fridays from 9am to 6pm. The respite room in the Sports Centre is a shared space and may be pre-booked for other uses. To enquire about booking outside of these hours please contact the Sports Centre via email on sport@tcd.ie. Please see the Trinity Sport Centre Respite Room Terms and Conditions for information on how to book and use the Sport Centre Respite Room.
food_drink_allowed_note: Please make sure to clean up after yourself and try to avoid any foodstuffs with strong smells.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: There is an assisted door to enter the room
seating_note: There are multiple types of different seating options, such as armchairs and a bed to rest on.
outlets_note: There are many sockets available for usage
sense_exp: This room is located adjacent to a sports hall, however, most noise tends to be blocked by the door. The train also goes by regularly which can be lightly heard and felt from the room. There are many variable lighting options available, the room also might have a more clinical-sterile smell to it because of the regular cleaning.
wayfinding:
The keys for the room can be picked up from the Sports Hall reception. You can ask someone there to escort you to the room. 

The room is located on the 2nd floor, you can either use the stairs of the lift, walk into a hall containing lots of posters of past students, turn left and enter a large room with an open sports hall on the story below, the room is on the right about halfway down the length of the hall. You will see the signage on the door, use the key to unlock the door.
phys_access: The room is accessible in all areas
further_info:
For more details about the Respite Space and how to access it, please refer to the Disability Service’s Respite Space [Information & Booking Page](https://www.tcd.ie/disability/support-and-resources/respite-space/). 

If you have any questions or require assistance with booking, please contact your Disability Officer directly or the Disability Service at askds@tcd.ie.

opening_times.note: This area can be booked through sport@tcd.ie

name: Health Centre Respite Room
description:
This is a room specifically for staff/students who experience pain or fatigue due to a disability (respite), or who are breastfeeding and would like a quiet space for this (parenting). It has seating, adjustable lighting, and a sink. This room can only be used by one person at a time, and can be booked online for one-hour slots by those using it as a respite space.  For more information on booking, 

College Health Respite Space is located just off the main reception area in the College Health Centre at Printing House Square and is available Monday to Friday from 9am to 1pm and 2pm to 4pm. The College Health Respite Space is provided only to students who have applied for supports with the DS. Only those who have been specifically referred for respite by their Disability Officer can access this room.

The College Health Respite Space must be booked in advance of use. Students are limited to 1 booking per day to ensure availability for other students. The College Health Respite Space can be booked through Online Booking Calendar the only.
food_drink_allowed_note: Please make sure to clean up after yourself and try to avoid any foodstuffs with strong smells.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6, or the Atrium.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: There is an assisted door to enter the room
seating_note: There are multiple types of different seating options, such as couches, a bed to rest on, and a rocking chair
outlets_note: There are many sockets available for usage
sense_exp: The room is deep under the Printing House Square building with nearly no external noise, except for a faint phone ringing from the health centre reception desk. The room has a clinical smell and is kept well clean and sterilised.
wayfinding:
The keys can picked up from the health centre reception desk, you can then ask someone to escort you to the room.

The room is located on the right as you go down the hall from the reception desk, signage can be found on the door.
phys_access: The room is accessible in all areas
further_info:
For more details about the Respite Space and how to access it, please refer to the Disability Service’s Respite Space [Information & Booking Page](https://www.tcd.ie/disability/support-and-resources/respite-space/). 

If you have any questions or require assistance with booking, please contact your Disability Officer directly or the Disability Service at askds@tcd.ie.

opening_times.note: This area can be booked through the Disability Service Booking Link.

name: Goldsmith Hall Society Rooms
description: Goldsmith Hall houses a variety of society rooms dedicated to supporting the diverse interests and activities of student groups. These spaces are equipped to cater to different needs, ranging from academic discussions to recreational activities. Each room within Goldsmith Hall is designed to provide an effective environment for society meetings, events, and gatherings. Juggling, Chess, DUMSS, Laurentian, Pirate, Engineering, Muslim, DUPSA, Zoo Soc, Werner Chemistry, VTP, Botanical, VDP, NetSoc.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are permitted in the rooms, making it convenient for longer meetings and events.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the Goldsmith SU Café or The Parlour.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the TBSI Zón Mac Léinn.
wheelchair_note: Goldsmith Hall is fully accessible to all students, with elevators and ramps ensuring ease of access to all society rooms.
seating_note: Each room features seating arrangements suited to its specific function, including tables, chairs, and flexible seating for various activities.
outlets_note: All rooms are equipped with power outlets to support electronic devices and equipment necessary for society functions.
sense_exp: Each room is designed to support the specific needs of the societies, with a focus on creating an environment conducive to their activities. The overall atmosphere is functional and welcoming.
wayfinding:
To find the Goldsmith Hall Society Rooms, enter Goldsmith Hall and follow the signs or campus map to locate the specific rooms designated for each society. The rooms are spread throughout the building, with clear signage to guide you.

[Youtube Video](https://youtu.be/-Re-aUur2iA)

opening_times.note: Access to Society Rooms may only be open to Society Members.

name: Enclosed Study Pods
description: If you prefer minimal visual stimuli, we have developed a number of areas with pods containing enclosed study desks. For example, there are two sets of quiet study pods on the Upper Level of the Lecky Library, which provide enclosure and reduced visual distraction, but also provide generous study space between each desk in an area with good natural light. If you want to work on assignments without any visual distractions, these pods are a great resource. Each pod has a comfortable chair and a desk, and is almost fully enclosed by a privacy screen.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The study pods are fully accessible and designed to accommodate all students. The Upper Level of the Lecky Library, where the pods are located, is accessible by both stairs and lift, ensuring ease of access for everyone.
seating_note: Each study pod is equipped with a comfortable padded chair and a desk, providing a generous and ergonomic study space. The layout of the pods ensures sufficient space between each desk, enhancing both privacy and concentration.
sense_exp:
The Enclosed Study Pods are designed to create a calm and focused atmosphere, making them suitable for students who are sensitive to visual and auditory stimuli. 

The pods are enclosed on three sides by privacy screens, which help to minimise visual distractions and create a sense of personal space. The area benefits from good natural light, providing a soft, even illumination that reduces eye strain. The library environment is generally quiet, with only minimal background noise, allowing you to concentrate fully on your work. 

The soft furnishings of the pods also contribute to a quieter ambience, absorbing sound and further reducing noise levels. This combination of factors makes the Enclosed Study Pods a comfortable and supportive environment for focused study sessions.
wayfinding:
You can use the internal library complex navigation tool to find this space and see how to get to it from one of the many entrances to the library complex.

You can find the location of the space within the library [here](https://app.cloudpano.com/tours/_JKNOIx10eo?sceneId=Qd9rIGif9C).
further_info:
[TCDSense, Trinity's Sensory Processing Project.](https://www.tcd.ie/disability/services/tcdsense.php) 

TCDSense aims to make Trinity College Dublin more inclusive, by creating a variety of different sensory environments to meet the needs of all students and staff across the various Trinity campuses. This involves reviewing and improving new and existing spaces across Trinity, creating increased awareness of the sensory environment amongst students and staff, and delivering specialist supports to students who need more support in managing and adapting the existing sensory environments of college.

name: Postgraduate Common Room
description:
The Postgrad Common Room in House 7 is a dedicated space for postgraduate students to unwind, study, and socialise. This space is split into two distinct areas: the common room itself and a fully equipped kitchen. The common room provides a comfortable and quiet environment with ample seating, while the kitchen is well-stocked with modern appliances, making it convenient for those who prefer to prepare their meals on campus. Both spaces offer a serene atmosphere, with large windows that bathe the rooms in natural light and offer picturesque views of College Green and Westmoreland Street. However, it’s important to note that the Postgrad Common Room is not fully accessible, as it is located on an upper floor accessible only by stairs.

[WC] There are gender-neutral bathrooms available.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are allowed in the common room, and the adjacent kitchen is well-equipped for meal preparation. The kitchen includes a sink, two microwaves, an oven, a hob, a fridge, a freezer, and a toaster, making it convenient for students who bring their own food or wish to prepare meals on-site.
microwave_note: Two microwaves are available in the kitchen area, providing a quick and easy way to heat up meals. The kitchen’s other amenities, including an oven and a hob, further enhance its utility for those who need to prepare or reheat food.
kettle_note: A kettle is available for students to use, making it convenient to prepare hot drinks like tea or coffee.
wheelchair_note: Unfortunately, the space is not fully accessible to all students. The room is located on an upper floor of House 7, which can only be accessed by stairs, as there is no lift available. While the building itself has ramp access and can be entered using a PG T-Card, the narrow corridors and the push/pull door system may pose challenges for some students.
seating_note: The common room is furnished with a variety of comfortable seating options, including five armchairs and four sofas, providing plenty of space for students to relax or engage in discussions. There is also a table available, making it a versatile space suitable for both informal meetings and solo study sessions.
outlets_note: The common room is equipped with several plug sockets, allowing students to easily charge their devices or work on their laptops while enjoying the comfortable surroundings.
sense_exp: The sensory experience in the Postgrad Common Room is one of calm and comfort. The room is filled with natural light from large windows that offer views of College Green and Westmoreland Street, creating a bright and inviting atmosphere. The tall ceilings and carpeted floor help to mute the acoustics, making the space relatively quiet, though noise from nearby traffic can sometimes filter in. The kitchen area is similarly well-lit, with a large window that overlooks College Green, adding to the room’s pleasant ambience.
wayfinding: To find the Postgrad Common Room in House 7, enter the building via the ramp and use your PG T-Card for access. Once inside, proceed up the stairs to the upper floor, navigating through a narrow corridor to reach the common room.
phys_access: The Postgrad Common Room is not fully accessible, as it requires stair access to reach the upper floor where the room is located. The building itself has ramp access, and entry is granted via a PG T-Card, but the narrow corridor leading to the common room and the push/pull door system may be difficult for some students to navigate. Additionally, there is no lift in the building, which restricts access to the room for those with mobility challenges.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)

opening_times.note: This area is only accessible to postgraduate students.

name: Resource Room
description: This is an attic room at the top of the GMB. The room is taken up by a large table and two smaller tables, with book cases and cabinets holding antique and more recent books across the walls. On both sides of the room there are wooden pillars that make up the eaves. There is a couch lining the back wall and chairs pulled up around the tables.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and Drink can be consumed in this area, there are no facilities for food/drink
wheelchair_note: This space is not Wheelchair accessible
seating_note: There is a high-backed couch wrapping the back of the room, as well as plenty of chairs.
outlets_note: There are 4 plug sockets, in the corners of the room, and behind the couch.
sense_exp: The room has two large windows at the far end of the room which allow for plenty of natural light, because it is on the top floor there is less street noise than other rooms in the GMB facing Front Square. There are overhead lights and one large standing lamp. The ceilings are lower and the floor is wood.
wayfinding: Walk up to the second floor of the GMB using the main staircase, go through the double doors on the left at the end of the landing, then go through the middle door directly facing those double doors, walk up the stairs, and at the end of the staircase take the door on your right.
phys_access: The room has large wooden pillars which make up the eaves of the building, which come up in the middle of the floor. The door can be heavy.

opening_times.note: This area is accessible for all students. Societies can book the space for events via the GMB jotform available on the CSC website.

name: Music Room
description: These rooms offer a quieter and more enclosed space, with pods providing individual study spaces to work in. These spaces are ideal if you want quiet areas to work, with lower levels of light and reduced visual distraction. If you prefer minimal visual stimuli, we have developed a number of areas with pods containing enclosed study desks. For example, there are two sets of quiet study pods on the Upper Level of the Lecky Library, which provide enclosure and reduced visual distraction, but also provide generous study space between each desk in an area with good natural light.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wayfinding: Please see location here: https://wagnerguide.com/c/trinitycollegedublin/ussher?animation=19096

[TCDSense, Trinity's Sensory Processing Project.](https://www.tcd.ie/disability/services/tcdsense.php) 

TCDSense aims to make Trinity College Dublin more inclusive, by creating a variety of different sensory environments to meet the needs of all students and staff across the various Trinity campuses. name: High Backed Seating
description: Numerous feedback surveys have highlighted that students value natural light, flexible seating and a connection to nature in their study environment. We have installed over thirty high-backed enclosed seats of various shapes, fabrics and colours throughout the libraries, in areas that provide these sensory characteristics.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
further_info:
[TCDSense, Trinity's Sensory Processing Project.](https://www.tcd.ie/disability/services/tcdsense.php) 

TCDSense aims to make Trinity College Dublin more inclusive, by creating a variety of different sensory environments to meet the needs of all students and staff across the various Trinity campuses. This involves reviewing and improving new and existing spaces across Trinity, creating increased awareness of the sensory environment amongst students and staff, and delivering specialist supports to students who need more support in managing and adapting the existing sensory environments of college.

name: SU Café
description: The SU Café Zón Mac Léinn is conveniently located just inside the door of Goldsmith Hall. It features many small tables and chairs, providing a cosy atmosphere for enjoying food and beverages. The café counter is operated by students, offering a variety of refreshments and light meals.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are welcome to bring your food to the café, you can also purchase food and drinks from the student-operated counter.
microwave_note: Available for student use, providing convenience for heating food.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the TBSI Zón Mac Léinn.
wheelchair_note: SU Café is fully accessible to all students. The arrangement of tables and seating helps clear main pathways and improves accessibility, especially during peak times of day.
seating_note: SU Café offers a variety of tables and chairs, creating a comfortable space for students to relax and socialise.
outlets_note: A few plug sockets are available throughout the café, mainly along the walls. Otherwise, The Parlour would be the nearest place for charging devices.
sense_exp: The café has a nice range of sensory experiences, some of the tables in the centre or nearer to the counter provide a lively and particularly bustling atmosphere during the day. Other tables along the walls, or in the corners and under the stairs are much quieter and tend to serve as great places to relax, study, or socialise more peacefully.
wayfinding: Enter the Goldsmith Hall and turn right, the SU Café counter can be seen a the back of the room, with many wooden tables & chairs filling the room before it.
phys_access: Goldsmith Hall is fully wheelchair accessible, with automatic doors facilitating entry into the building. The café itself is designed with accessibility in mind, featuring smooth linoleum flooring and ample space between seating arrangements to ensure ease of movement for all students. The nearby amenities, including microwaves and water fountains, are positioned at accessible heights, ensuring that everyone can use the facilities comfortably.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)

name: The Parlour
description: The Parlour is a Zón Mac Léinn located on the ground floor of Goldsmith Hall, just along the corridor beside the SU Café. It offers a couple of microwaves to heat food, lots of comfortable seating options, and a couple of pool tables. While it can get quite noisy around lunchtime, making it less ideal for studying, it is perfect for meeting friends for lunch and socialising.
food_drink_allowed_note: You can bring and consume food and drink in the Parlour. There are also a couple of microwaves available for heating your food.
microwave_note: Available for student use.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the TBSI Zón Mac Léinn.
wheelchair_note: The Parlour is fully accessible to all students.
seating_note: The Parlour offers a variety of comfortable seating options including couches, bean bags, and stools, making it an ideal spot to relax and socialise.
outlets_note: The Parlour offers a variety of comfortable seating options including couches, bean bags, and stools, making it an ideal spot to relax and socialise.
sense_exp: The Parlour can be quite noisy, especially around lunchtime, due to the social nature of the space and the presence of pool tables. It is a lively environment, perfect for social interactions.
wayfinding: When entering Goldsmith Hall, walk through the SU Café, and go towards the double doors to the right of the Café counter, walk through a short hallway until a door appears on your left that opens to a room filled with Pool tables, sensory seating, and large blue high-back couches.
phys_access: The Parlour is fully accessible to all students, furniture can be moved and might be challenging to navigate if left in a poor state.
further_info:
This space is a Zón Mac Léinn operated by the TCD-SU / AML-CT.

To find out more about your SU / AML see [here](https://www.tcdsu.org/)org/)

name: The Eliz Room
description: The Eliz Room is a spacious meeting room located in House 6, designed for hosting society events and gatherings. It offers a seating capacity of 20 individuals, with additional standing room for 10 more attendees. Positioned adjacent to the CSC Office, this room features large individual seats and a long, continuous table that extends throughout the space. Please note that access to this room requires climbing a staircase as it is located on the 1st floor of the building.
food_drink_allowed_note: You are permitted to consume food and beverages within the Eliz Room. However, please ensure that any refreshments brought into the room are disposed of responsibly after use.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note: The upper floors of House 6 are not physically accessible.
seating_note: The Eliz Room provides ample seating arrangements, including individual seats and a long table that accommodates all attendees comfortably during society events.
outlets_note: There are multiple plug sockets available within the Eliz Room to facilitate the use of electronic devices and equipment during meetings and events.
wayfinding: To locate the Eliz Room, proceed to House 6 and head upstars towards the CSC Office. The Eliz Room is adjacent to the CSC Office. Look-out for signage indicating its location.

opening_times.note: This area can be booked through the CSC.

name: Indoor Tropical Garden
description: The Indoor Tropical Garden is a peaceful and secluded space designed for quiet reflection, relaxation, and study. Located within a building surrounded by offices, this unique garden features large tropical plants that create a calming, green oasis indoors. The area is designed to be tranquil, with a focus on natural beauty and serenity. The space provides an ideal environment for students who need a break from their studies or just want to spend time in a calming atmosphere
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drinks are permitted in the Indoor Tropical Garden, please dispose of your rubbish properly to maintain the cleanliness and serenity of the space.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the JCR Hamilton.
wheelchair_note: This space is not physically accessible as you will need to navigate a narrow spiral staircase to get down to the ground floor level.
seating_note: There are two comfortable benches at the centre of the garden, positioned amidst the lush plant life, offering students a quiet place to sit, read, or unwind.
outlets_note: There are no plug sockets available in this space, keeping the focus on nature and peace. Students should charge devices elsewhere.
primary_image_alt: Large tropical plants with benches at the centre
sense_exp: The space offers a visually immersive experience with tall tropical plants that create a sense of calm. The natural shades of green and earthy tones dominate the surroundings, providing a soothing colour palette. The atmosphere is quiet, with the faint sound of leaves rustling in the indoor breeze. The space is designed to be free from loud noises or disturbances, making it a sensory-friendly environment. The smell of plants and fresh soil adds to the sensory richness of this tranquil area.
wayfinding: The Indoor Tropical Garden is located within the building and is easy to find. Upon entering the School of Computer Science and Statistics pass by the office and continue down the hall until you reach the open concourse area which hosts the garden.

name: The Atrium Rooms 2, 3, and 4
description: The Atrium Rooms 2, 3, and 4 are versatile spaces commonly used for a variety of society events. These rooms include the Workshop Room (Atrium Room 2), the Meeting Room (Atrium Room 3), and the Conversation Space (Atrium Room 4). Located within the Atrium building, these rooms offer a convenient setting for student societies to host workshops, meetings, and social gatherings. The space also features a kitchen on the first floor, equipped with essential amenities including microwaves and a sink.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drink are generally allowed in these rooms. The kitchen on the first floor provides additional convenience with microwaves and a sink for preparing and cleaning up food and beverages. Please ensure that all food and drink items are cleared away after your event to maintain a clean space.
microwave_note: There are two microwaves available on the first floor of the Atrium building. To access them, head up the stairs and through the door located directly above Atrium Room 2. These microwaves are available for use by all those hosting events in the Atrium Rooms.
kettle_note: The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
wheelchair_note:
The Atrium building is fully accessible to all students. You can find the lift in the corner of the Atrium Hall.

Most doors are automated, doors to the three atrium rooms are not.
seating_note: Each room is designed to accommodate different types of events. The Workshop Room (Atrium Room 2) is set up with tables and chairs suitable for hands-on activities and collaborative work. The Meeting Room (Atrium Room 3) provides a more formal seating arrangement ideal for discussions and presentations. The Conversation Space (Atrium Room 4) features comfortable seating options for casual chats and networking. Seating can be rearranged to suit the needs of your event.
outlets_note: Each room is equipped with a number of plug sockets to support various electronic devices and equipment used during events. This allows for the easy setup of presentations, laptops, and other essential tech.
sense_exp: The Atrium Rooms feature a functional design with a neutral aesthetic. The long and narrow configuration of the rooms can amplify sound, making the space particularly lively during midday events when multiple societies might be using the rooms simultaneously. The kitchen area on the first floor provides natural lighting and a practical environment for meal preparation.
wayfinding: To find the Atrium Rooms, enter the Atrium building and proceed to the first floor. The rooms are clearly marked, with Atrium Room 2, Atrium Room 3, and Atrium Room 4 situated adjacent to each other. For access to the kitchen, follow the stairs up to the first floor and navigate through the door directly above Atrium Room 2.
phys_access: The Atrium building is equipped with accessible entry points, including ramps.
aka: Atrium Room 2, Atrium room 3, Atrium room 4, Seomraí Aitriam

opening_times.note: These areas can be booked through the CSC.

name: TAP Student Offices
description: Trinity Access Programmes (TAP) supports students who enter TCD through the HEAR scheme, the Foundation Course, or other University Access Routes linked with TCD. TAP aims to support individuals from underrepresented areas to reach their full educational potential. TAP students have the opportunity to avail themselves of a number of academic and financial supports during their Undergraduate studies. The Studio is a learning centre for the Foundation Course and HEAR students. It is located in Goldsmith Hall (TAP Student Offices) and has access to networked computers and printers. The Studio is a good place to work either on your own or with a group. For more information, please contact tapundergraduates@tcd.ie.
seating_note: seating for 25 with tables
outlets_note: Plug sockets available
sense_exp: Windows on two sides of the space.
wayfinding: The space (M48) is located within the TAP student offices. Enter Goldsmith Hall and take the stairs, turn left and follow the TAP signs along the corridor.
phys_access: All doors to the space are automatic. There is a lift to the first floor to the let of the stairs.

opening_times.note: contact tapundergraduates@tcd.ie for more information

name: ATIC Space Ussher
description: The ATIC (Assistive Technology and Information Centre) Space, located within the Ussher Library, is a designated study area for students registered with the Disability Service. It offers a mix of individual and shared study spaces designed to provide an accessible and comfortable learning environment. The space includes two individual study rooms for private, focused study, as well as a shared study space with six desks and an open-plan area. The study desks in the open-plan area come equipped with desktop screens to create a more enclosed, distraction-free workspace. This environment caters to a wide range of study needs and promotes inclusivity.
food_drink_allowed_note: Food and drinks are not permitted in the ATIC Space to maintain a clean and distraction-free environment.
microwave_note: The nearest microwave from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
kettle_note:
The nearest kettle from here can be found in the SU Kitchen in House 6.
.
wheelchair_note: The ATIC Space is fully accessible to all students, with a particular focus on the needs of students registered with the disability service.
seating_note: There are many seating options, including ergonomic chairs at the study desks and more casual seating in the shared areas. The two individual study pods provide comfortable, enclosed seating for students who require privacy.
outlets_note: Each desk is equipped with multiple plug sockets, allowing students to charge their laptops, phones, and other devices while they study.
sense_exp: The ATIC Space has been designed to create a quiet, calm study environment. The individual study pods provide a sense of enclosure and reduce external visual distractions. The open-plan area, while offering some exposure to others, is still enclosed with desktop screens to maintain privacy. The overall space benefits from soft, natural lighting and muted colours that contribute to a calming atmosphere. The area is designed to minimise noise, making it suitable for students who are sensitive to sensory overload.
wayfinding:
You can use the internal library complex navigation tool to find this space and see how to get to it from one of the many entrances to the library complex.

You can find the location of the space within the library [here](https://app.cloudpano.com/tours/_JKNOIx10eo?sceneId=-ZjSqueRzV).
phys_access: The ATIC Space is fully accessible for students with mobility needs. The library building has lift access, and the pathways within the space are wide and unobstructed. The desks are adjustable, and there is plenty of room between them for comfortable movement. The individual study rooms are also accessible, with doors that are easy to open and close.
further_info:
There are two sensory rooms for individual low-distraction study in the Assistive Technology Information Centre (ATIC) on the ground floor of the Ussher Library. Each room has a height adjustable desk with power and is accessible to wheelchair users (note: the doors are not fully automated).
